survivors.title: The pass-3 "unmodelled answer keys" report is re-derived from the stored record instead of read from it, so it prints the builder's own bookkeeping fields as things the model said.
lenses: Values computed and never read — exported functions with no non-test caller, object fields populated on a write path and read on no path, and computed results discarded by the one consumer that wanted them.
doctrine 6 — never drop anything silently
survivors.why: matchComplete.ts:200-218 calls this list "where a hypothesis lands first" and "the specification for the channel" — the evidence from which the unbuilt hypothesis channel is to be designed. The script's own header says "a bucket that is reported into a variable nobody prints is the same drop one layer up, so it is printed here" — and then prints a different, wrong list. A run on real data will report eight keys on every visit, including `unmodelledKeys` itself, so the genuine signal (a model key this build has no home for) is indistinguishable from noise, and the real one is never read at all.
survivors.evidence:
`normaliseMatch` computes the value (server/src/ai/tasks/matchComplete.ts:448):

    const MODELLED = new Set(['located', 'couldNotLocate', 'additional', 'unsure'])
    const unmodelledKeys = Object.entries(output as unknown as Record<string, unknown>)
      .filter(([k]) => !MODELLED.has(k))

It is stored: `recordGeneration({ ..., output: stored, ... })` → `JSON.stringify(args.output)` (server/src/ai/queue.ts:398). `grep -rn "unmodelledKeys" server/scripts server/src/index.ts web/src` returns NOTHING — no reader anywhere.

The only place that reports the signal recomputes it over the WRONG object (server/scripts/match.ts:151-166):

    `SELECT output FROM ai_generations WHERE ... task IN ('match_known','enumerate_room')`
    const MODELLED = new Set(['located', 'couldNotLocate', 'additional', 'unsure'])
    for (const [k, v] of Object.entries(o)) { if (MODELLED.has(k) || seen.has(k)) continue; seen.set(k, ...) }
    console.log(`\n⚑ ${seen.size} answer key(s) this build does not model. NOTHING here became an object:`)

`output` holds a `StoredMatch` (12 top-level keys), not the model's `MatchOutput` (5). Replaying that exact loop over a StoredMatch:

    $ node -e '...same loop over a StoredMatch...'
    ⚑ 8 answer key(s) this build does not model. NOTHING here became an object:
        question: match_known
        evidenceless: []
        unmodelledKeys: [{"key":"roomNote",...}]
        roomNote: a tidy mechanical room
        unknownProducts: []
        unknownClasses: []
        strayEvidence: []
        danglingParents: []

Second defect inside the same value: `MODELLED` at matchComplete.ts:448 omits `roomNote`, which IS a modelled field (`MatchOutput.roomNote`, line 186), so every match generation's stored `unmodelledKeys` carries a false entry.
corrections:
The finding stands. Two corrections, one narrowing and one widening.

NARROWING — the falsification recipe names a flag that does not exist. There is no `--report`. Argument parsing is at match.ts:130-134, and `reportUnmodelled()` is called at match.ts:176, below the plan-only early exit at match.ts:94-98 (`if (!flag('run')) { ...; report(); process.exit(0) }`). So the plan-only path prints `report()` and never `reportUnmodelled()`. The correct command is `npm run match -- --visit <id> --run --owner-property`, which sends a live paid run. Observing the defect therefore costs a model call — which is itself part of why it has gone unseen.

WIDENING — the genuine signal is worse off than the finding says. `possibleDuplicates`, the only key in my probe that the build actually has no home for, is NOT printed as its own row. `normaliseMatch` drops it from the returned object; it survives only inside the `unmodelledKeys` field, whose preview the script truncates to 160 chars (match.ts:165) on top of the 200-char truncation already applied at matchComplete.ts:452. So the report does not merely bury the signal among seven bookkeeping rows — with more than one unmodelled key, or one of any length, the real content is cut off mid-string and lost. The one thing the mechanism exists to surface is the one thing the print can silently drop.

Also worth recording: `unknownProducts`, `unknownClasses`, `strayEvidence`, `danglingParents` and `evidenceless` are computed and stored by normaliseMatch and are printed nowhere else in match.ts either — I read the whole of `report()` (match.ts:180-221) and it prints only objects, lanes and class coverage. They currently reach a reader only as the empty-array rows in this same broken list.

The finding stands as stated; two corrections to its edges.

1. The falsification recipe names a flag that does not exist. There is no `--report` in server/scripts/match.ts; the flags are `--visit`, `--zone`, `--run`, `--owner-property`, `--tier`, `--limit`, `--again` (arg/flag helpers at match.ts:30-35). More importantly, reportUnmodelled() at match.ts:176 is only reachable after a live drain: the plan-only branch at match.ts:92-97 calls `report()` then `process.exit(0)` before it. Correct repro: `npm run match -- --visit <id> --run --owner-property`. So the wrong list prints only inside a paid run's output, never on the free plan-only invocation a person would use to re-read a visit — which makes it less likely to be noticed, not more.

2. Worth adding, with a caveat. MATCH_SCHEMA sets `additionalProperties: false` (matchComplete.ts:87) and is passed as a structured-output constraint (`output_config: { format: { type: 'json_schema', schema: args.schema } }`, server/src/ai/client.ts:170). If the provider enforces that strictly — I verified the wiring, not the provider's runtime behaviour — then the model cannot return a key outside the five, so the genuine signal unmodelledKeys was built to collect is structurally unreachable through this path and the only entry it can ever hold is the false `roomNote` one. That would make the "hypothesis channel's specification writing itself" (matchComplete.ts:200-218) a bucket that can collect nothing real while guaranteeing one wrong entry per generation. Falsifiable: a run against the live API with a prompt inviting an extra key either yields it in unmodelledKeys or is stripped by the schema.

survivors.title: The §1h.1 zone-audit correctness oracle never runs on real data — `auditZones` has no caller outside tests.
lenses: Values computed and never read — exported functions with no non-test caller, object fields populated on a write path and read on no path, and computed results discarded by the one consumer that wanted them.
survivors.why: This is described as the one place in the repo with an independent right answer — two implementations of the same applicability logic on the same house. The header records that it was silently wrong for four increments and that only real data exposed it. Today no real import can expose anything: an operator imports a visit, the field app's `coreUnresolved`/`standardUnresolved`/`naCount` are echoed back to them, and a divergence in the engine's trigger evaluation is never computed. `facts.ts:222` even emits a warning telling the operator "The zone-audit oracle compares applicability against the field app on every closed zone; check it" — pointing at a comparison that does not run.
survivors.evidence:
The module header claims it runs everywhere:

    * Which means **the engine's applicability logic can be checked against every
    * zone of every import, for free, with a known right answer.**
    * Any divergence is a real bug, in the engine, the config, or the field app. It
    * is surfaced, never papered over.

The comparison it produces (zoneAudit.ts:101-109):

    export interface ZoneComparison {
      ...
      agrees: boolean
      /** Every difference, named. A count alone cannot be chased. */
      differences: string[]
    }

`grep -rn "auditZones" server/src server/scripts web/src` → only `server/test/audit.test.ts`, `server/test/walk-fixture.test.ts`, `server/test/sections-4-and-7.test.ts`. `activeItems.ts:46` imports only `inScope` and `listsForZoneType` from this module, not the comparison. An import-graph walk from every entry point (server/src/index.ts, web/src/main.tsx, all 15 server/scripts/*.ts, the golden runners, operators/cli.ts) does not reach zoneAudit.ts at all.

The only production reader of `zones.audit_summary` displays the field app's numbers verbatim without comparing (server/src/import/report.ts:210-243).
corrections:
Two wording fixes, both narrowing rather than weakening.

1. "Never runs on real data" overstates it. It runs on every `npm test` against two genuinely real archived exports — including the 8-zone walk that exposed the four-increment fold bug (`walk-fixture.test.ts:50`, `audit.test.ts:258`). What it never runs on is an operator's import. The accurate statement: the oracle has no caller outside the test suite, so it can only ever compare the two frozen fixtures, never a newly imported visit — which is the case its own header says was the one that caught the bug, and the case a new field-app config version would arrive in.

2. Add the sharpest single consequence, which the evidence given only gestures at: the tests pass a hardcoded `'baseline'` (audit.test.ts:258, walk-fixture.test.ts:50), so the required-`visitKind` wall at zoneAudit.ts:274-277 — "A default of `baseline` would quietly produce a correct-looking answer for a monthly visit, and the whole value of this oracle is that a wrong answer is visible" — is a guard on a parameter no production caller ever supplies. Meanwhile `server/src/index.ts:160` does exactly what that comment forbids for the audit run (`visitKind: triggering?.kind ?? 'baseline'`), which is a defended default, not the same defect.

Two factual corrections. (a) The import-graph claim "does not reach zoneAudit.ts at all" is false. I walked imports from server/src/index.ts, web/src/main.tsx and all 15 server/scripts/*.ts: 107 modules reached, and zoneAudit.ts IS among them — pulled in by server/src/audit/activeItems.ts:46, `import { inScope, listsForZoneType, type ChecklistItem } from './zoneAudit.js'`, which runs in production via runAudit's v3 `fromConfig` path. The module loads; what is never called is `auditZones` (zoneAudit.ts:278) and its private `compare()` (zoneAudit.ts:356). Accurate statement: the oracle's applicability helpers ARE production code, so a corruption there would silently move live gap counts — and the one check that could catch it never runs. (b) "Never runs on real data" overstates: the oracle does run against a real (redacted) export in the test suite — walk-fixture.test.ts:50, eight zones, seventeen pins, the fixture cut precisely because the reference export could not exercise it. The precise claim is: `auditZones` never runs on an import an operator performs; no route, script, or run path calls it, so the comparison exists only inside `npm test` against the two archived fixtures. Also, the operator-facing warning is at facts.ts:217, not 222.

survivors.title: `RoomKey.unconfirmed_objects` is in the committed ground truth and read by nothing, so proposals matching the key's own "possible" entries are scored as false positives.
lenses: Values computed and never read — exported functions with no non-test caller, object fields populated on a write path and read on no path, and computed results discarded by the one consumer that wanted them.
survivors.why: The false-positive count is the number the identification passes are judged on, and the report's own note justifies it by saying the owner attested the key complete for existence. The key is not complete in that sense — it carries a second list of things the owner saw and could not confirm, and a proposal landing on one of those is the engine agreeing with the owner, not inventing something. Rule 5 ("every disagreement is resolvable in both directions") cannot operate on a category the scorer cannot see. Eight of the nine entries share photographs with confirmed objects and so are absorbed by accident; the ninth is disjoint and lands straight in `falsePositives`.
survivors.evidence:
Declared:

    export interface RoomKey {
      confirmed_objects: KeyObject[]
      unconfirmed_objects?: { proposal?: string; photographs: string[] }[]
      readings?: unknown[]
    }

Populated — `fixtures/room-records/mechanical-room_2026-08-10.json:553` carries 9 entries ("Possible well-pump pressure switch / electrical control", "Possible legacy telephone terminal / distribution block", …). `grep -rn unconfirmed_objects server` returns exactly two hits: this type line and the fixture.

`scoreRun` never mentions it (score.ts:549-551):

    const falsePositives = proposals
      .filter((p) => !claimed.has(p.id))
      .map((p) => ({ id: p.id, label: p.label, classId: p.classId, lane: laneOf(p) }))

Demonstrated with tsx against the real key:

    confirmed_objects: 34
    unconfirmed_objects: 9
    proposal reproducing the KEY'S OWN unconfirmed entry verbatim:
    [ { "id": "probe", "label": "Possible legacy telephone terminal / distribution block",
        "classId": null, "lane": "appearance" } ]
    note: ... 1 proposal(s) matched no key object; those are scoreable only because
          the owner attested the key complete for existence.
corrections:
The finding stands, but its headline overstates the blast radius and should be narrowed to what I measured.

MEASURED, not asserted. Of the 9 entries, 8 name at least one photograph that a confirmed object also names, so proposals citing them are absorbed into `claimed` (score.ts:421) and never reach `falsePositives` — they surface instead as "got:" lines under some confirmed object's disagreement. Exactly ONE photograph in the whole key — `019fb977-e4b2-7398-98fc-a498cecf5a7c`, the legacy telephone terminal — is named only by an unconfirmed entry. So today precisely one frame of the key's 58 can produce this false positive.

AND IT HAS NEVER FIRED. Against the committed real run (`fixtures/proposals/mechanical-room_pass3_2026-08-13.json`, 80 proposals), zero proposals cite that photograph, and zero proposals cite no confirmed photograph at all. The single false positive in the published run was `Pressurized bladder tank isolation hardware` with `mediaIds: []` (Note_First-Pass-3-Run_2026-08-13.md:70, since refused into an `evidenceless` bucket). No published number is wrong. This is latent, not realised.

THE ACCURATE STATEMENT OF THE DEFECT. `keyObjects` and `falsePositives` are derived from `confirmed_objects` alone (score.ts:419, 550-556), while the justification printed beside them — score.ts:566-567, "scoreable only because the owner attested the key complete for existence" — invokes an attestation over the whole record, of which the scorer reads one of three arrays. score.ts:4-7 states the precondition for the strong verdict and names the weak one ("merely unaccounted for") that the second list should trigger; nothing computes which applies. A reader of the report cannot tell that the key lists the thing the engine just proposed, and rule 5 ("every disagreement is resolvable in both directions") needs the human to see the disagreement to resolve it.

This is the signature shape in its ground-truth form: the value is committed to version control by the owner's own 2026-08-11 ruling and no reader of the report can reach it.

The headline over-generalizes; the finder's own body has it right. Only 1 of the 9 unconfirmed entries becomes a false positive — "Possible legacy telephone terminal / distribution block", whose single photograph is disjoint from every confirmed object. The other 8 share photographs with confirmed objects, so `for (const h of hits) claimed.add(h.id)` (score.ts:421) absorbs them and they never reach `falsePositives`. That absorption is a second, separate mis-scoring rather than a harmless one: an absorbed proposal is counted among a confirmed object's `hits`, and where it is the only hit the object is judged `wrong` (score.ts:544, "N proposal(s) cite this object's photographs and none matches the role") for naming a thing the owner also saw and could not confirm. State the defect precisely as the gap between the stated semantic and the implementation: score.ts:264 ("Proposals matching no key object at all."), score.ts:291 (same wording on the per-lane tally) and scripts/score.ts:251 ("Proposals matching no key object") all claim the whole key, while `falsePositives` at score.ts:549-551 is computed against `claimed`, which is built only from `key.confirmed_objects` (score.ts:419). The number therefore means "matching no CONFIRMED key object", and the report's own justification — the owner's attestation that the key is complete for existence — is the attestation of a file that carries a second list of things that exist and are unnamed.

survivors.title: The AI accuracy record and the golden-set growth query are computed, tested, and reachable by no route, screen, or script.
lenses: Values computed and never read — exported functions with no non-test caller, object fields populated on a write path and read on no path, and computed results discarded by the one consumer that wanted them.
survivors.why: CLAUDE.md §9 makes `ai_generations` the improvement data as well as the ledger, and accept.ts:481-496 says the golden set "grows by absorbing the real failures, and this is the query that finds them". Neither growth nor measurement can happen: after a real visit nobody can see how often the model was right, and the edits and discards that would become golden-set entries sit in the table with no way to list them. The data is being accumulated for a reader that does not exist.
corrections: A narrower residual survives, and it is not what was claimed. Two specific things have no reader at all: (a) a discarded generation vanishes entirely — pendingProposals filters `human_decision = 'pending'` (accept.ts:405) and the web joins provenance only onto accepted overlays (Assist.tsx:623) — while accept.ts:8-11 insists "DISCARD IS RECORDED, NEVER DELETED... the discards are the evidence"; and (b) goldenCandidates is the collection half of a flow ratification.ts:11-13 calls distributed ("every visit can contribute a candidate") whose listing half does not exist. Two asymmetries are worth noting for a future pass: visitSpend (queue.ts:252) is the same shape of aggregate over the same table and is wired into screen.ts, and golden-standing.ts:1-17 exists precisely because a number "only ever seen by someone who already went looking" was judged a defect. So the accurate statement is not "computed and reachable by no route" but "the aggregate count and the discard list are unbuilt readers that carry no label" — which under CLAUDE.md §15's own rule is answered by a labelled row, not by a route.

One precision fix, which narrows the claim without killing it: the accept/edit diff is NOT wholly invisible to a person. `web/src/pass/Assist.tsx:624-641` renders, per accepted value on the pin currently open, `read from the photo, edited by you ... the model read {priorValue}` — so a concierge standing on one pin can see that one reading was corrected. But that is per-value, live-state-only, sourced from the overlay rather than `ai_generations`, and it has no aggregate and no cross-pin or cross-visit listing; discards appear nowhere at all (their `discard` overlay, accept.ts:286, is written and never read). So the accurate statement is: the per-value diff is visible one pin at a time in the pass; the visit-level accuracy record (`accuracy`, accept.ts:552) and the golden-set growth query (`goldenCandidates`, accept.ts:498) have no non-test caller — no route, no screen model, no script.

survivors.title: `confirmObject` — the only writer of `objects.confirmed_by` — has no production caller, and the module's own defence names the wrong half as idle.
lenses: Values computed and never read — exported functions with no non-test caller, object fields populated on a write path and read on no path, and computed results discarded by the one consumer that wanted them.
survivors.why: "The desk proposes, a person confirms" has no reachable path. `scripts/identify.ts:375` prints "None is confirmed — that is the next act, and it is a human's" and there is no act available: no route, no CLI command, no screen. The defence in the header is precise about `adopted` and silently implies the `confirmed` path is wired and has a click behind it; neither is true, so a reader auditing this file concludes the confirmation surface exists.
survivors.evidence:
export function confirmObject(db: Db, args: ConfirmArgs): ConfirmResult {
      const object = db.prepare('SELECT id, class_id FROM objects WHERE id = ?')...
      ...
      db.prepare('UPDATE objects SET confirmed_by = ?, confirmed_at = ? WHERE id = ?')

`grep -rn confirmObject server web` → only `server/test/engine-confirm.test.ts` and `server/test/identification.test.ts`. The import graph from every entry point never reaches `server/src/engine/confirm.ts`. `objects` is written with `confirmed_by` NULL by both passes (identify.ts:731, matchComplete.ts:556) and read by no API route (`grep -n "FROM objects" server/src/index.ts` → nothing).

The header defends only one half:

    * **The `adopted` path has no production caller yet**, because §4's research pass
    * is not built ... It is constructed in tests and nowhere else
    * **The workflow is unchanged — one click per object, never twelve.**
corrections: The accurate residue is narrow and documentary rather than a defect in the mechanism: confirm.ts:22's heading "What is idle here, said plainly" is literally incomplete — by rule 11's own framing it should name two idlenesses, not one. Nothing calls `confirmObject` at all, and no production code reads objects.confirmed_by, object_decisions or object_provenance; the `adopted` branch is additionally idle for a second reason (no research pass to supply `derived[]`). One added clause — "the whole module awaits stage 10's desk screen; the adopted half additionally awaits §4's research pass" — would make the header say plainly what its heading promises. That is a wording gap in a module whose non-invocation is already recorded in the stage table, not a computed value a reader cannot reach.

Two adjustments, neither of which touches the core.

1. FILE PATHS IN THE EVIDENCE ARE WRONG. The NULL-hardcoding inserts are at `server/src/ai/tasks/identify.ts:731` and `server/src/ai/tasks/matchComplete.ts:556`, not `server/src/engine/`. (`server/src/engine/identify.ts` is a different file.) The line numbers are right.

2. NARROW THE "SILENTLY IMPLIES A CLICK" HALF. "**The workflow is unchanged — one click per object, never twelve.**" is fairly read as comparing Amendment 1 §B's design against a per-output alternative, not as asserting a built screen; leaning on it weakens the finding. The load-bearing defect is the section heading immediately below it: `## What is idle here, said plainly` promises an enumeration and names one half — "**The `adopted` path has no production caller yet** ... It is constructed in tests and nowhere else" — when `confirmObject` itself, the `confirmed` path included, is constructed in tests and nowhere else. The sentence is true and the section is not. This repo has the convention available and uses it elsewhere: `server/src/audit/sources.ts:12` says plainly "**Most of these are not wired yet, and that is** ..." — confirm.ts applies it to one branch and not to the module.

WORTH ADDING: the finding understates the reach. It is not only that `confirmed_by` has no writer a person can trigger — `object_decisions` and `object_provenance`, the two tables migration 018 exists for, are read by nothing in production either. Nothing gates a render, a binder draft or a session plan on an object having been confirmed, so the doctrine "nothing renders until signed" is, for objects, neither enforceable nor enforced.

survivors.title: CONFIRMED (known instance): all five exports of `audit/provenance.ts` — the §1g.1 unverifiable-provenance machinery — are imported only by their own test.
lenses: Values computed and never read — exported functions with no non-test caller, object fields populated on a write path and read on no path, and computed results discarded by the one consumer that wanted them.

Declared in a schema/config and consumed by nothing — every field, column, and vocabulary term in `/schema/*.json`, `server/src/db/migrations/*.sql`, and the import config snapshot, traced to a reader.
survivors.why: `Verification` ('verified' | 'unverifiable' | 'unknown-provenance') is the mechanism that stops an unverifiable install year re-entering a fleet view looking photographed. Nothing in the audit run, the gap report, the pass model or the binder draft calls `verify`, so no value anywhere in the running system carries a verification state, and `describeProvenance`'s honest sentence is never produced. Confirmed as the seed instance rather than a new one.
survivors.evidence:
Exports: `provenanceMap` (81), `verify` (126), `aggregate` (214), `mergeBreakdowns` (234), `describeProvenance` (249).

    $ grep -rn "audit/provenance" server/src server/scripts web/src
    server/src/report/renderGate.ts:20: * **That is Table I** — `audit/provenance.ts`, five exported functions built,

That is a comment, not an import. The only real importer is `server/test/provenance.test.ts:25`. The repo already names it: renderGate.ts:19-23 — "five exported functions built, tested, and called by nothing, idle for weeks with no test able to notice."
corrections: The finding stands; only its falsification recipe names the wrong field. Table I is keyed on *derived* values, not on the plate reading itself: the walk export's eight rows are `wh.age`, `ft.age`, `apw.hose-age`, `wsf.age`, `pnl.service`, `pnl.brand` and two more — `wh.serial` is not among them. So `verify({valueItem: 'wh.serial'})` would return `unknown-provenance` ("this config declares no capturing photo item for wh.serial"), not `unverifiable`. The correct test is: import `fixtures/walk-2026-07-31/` (the reference export declares no `provenance` key at all, so it cannot exercise this), find a pin where `wh.nameplate` resolved `na / none-present`, and look for any output describing the water heater's **age / install year** as unverifiable. There is none. Also worth stating precisely: today the observable loss is not merely a missing flag — the export ships Table I, the import stores it verbatim, and no code path reads `snapshot.provenance`, so the eight declared relationships are carried into the database and never consulted.

The finding stands as stated; one detail makes it stronger and should be added. The dead chain is one node longer than the claim describes: `PropertyEvidence.pinResolutions` — server/src/audit/propertyEvidence.ts:139, commented "Latest state per (pin, item) — §1g.1 ... Table I asks whether it was satisfied *on this pin*", populated at propertyEvidence.ts:323-376 on every audit run — is the purpose-built input to `verify(args.pinResolutions)`. Its only non-test consumer is server/src/plan/sessionPlan.ts:416 (`const resolution = evidence.pinResolutions.get(pin.pinId)?.get(itemId)`), which uses it for an unrelated job: finding a prior unit photograph for the session plan, checking only `resolution?.kind !== 'satisfied'`. So the co-visibility map §1g.1 required is computed on every run and never once reaches the function it exists for.

survivors.title: `freeformLabelProposals` — the review queue built specifically because "nobody counts it" — is counted by nothing.
lenses: Values computed and never read — exported functions with no non-test caller, object fields populated on a write path and read on no path, and computed results discarded by the one consumer that wanted them.
survivors.why: The header's own table of measured labels (`Receptacle` 2 + 6 across the two real exports, `Ceiling stains`, `Zone notes`, `Return`) is the evidence the class frame should grow — and it was produced by hand, not by a surface anyone can open. `properties` (labels appearing at more than one house) is described as "the number that matters most" and no human can obtain it without writing a script. The failure the module names as its reason for existing is still the current state.
survivors.evidence:
/**
     * **The named failure:** *the class list is written once from imagination and
     * never grows, because the evidence that it should grow sits in the exports and
     * nobody counts it.*
     * Freeform pin labels ... have been **exported verbatim and flagged since the
     * Manifest Contract was written**, and nothing has ever aggregated them.
     */
    export function freeformLabelProposals(db: Db, opts: { propertyId?: string } = {}): LabelReview {

`grep -rn "freeformLabelProposals\|reviewQueue" server web` outside the module → only `server/test/engine-confirm.test.ts` (6 call sites). No API route, no page, no `server/scripts/*.ts`. The whole module is unreachable from every entry point.
corrections:
Two refinements, neither of which saves the finding.

"Counted by nothing" is right about aggregation but slightly overstated about visibility. Individual freeform labels DO reach one screen, unaggregated: `server/src/audit/binding.ts:294-295` sets `describedAs: pin.componentType ?? pin.freeformLabel ?? 'no type recorded'` with `reason: ... : pin.freeformLabel ? 'freeform' : 'typeless'`, and `web/src/pages/Audit.tsx:471-472` renders it as `pin ${e.number} — ${e.describedAs} (${e.reason})`. So a human can see "Receptacle" one pin at a time, in one property's audit — never grouped, never counted, never across houses.

And that path makes the finding worse rather than better in one respect. `binding.ts:286` filters `.filter((pin) => !pin.retired && !boundPins.has(pin.pinId))` — retired pins are dropped. reviewQueue.ts:31-34 exists in part to forbid exactly that: "**Retired pins are counted and marked, never dropped.** The reason a concierge retired a pin is data — a label that keeps being typed and keeps being retired is a different signal from one that sticks — and doctrine 6 forbids the silent drop either way." The only reachable view of freeform labels is the one that makes the drop the module was written to prevent.

Third supporting detail: `server/src/import/report.ts:74` declares `freeform_label: string | null` and line 79 selects it, and `grep -n freeform server/src/import/report.ts` shows those two lines only — it is never emitted. The pins block reports `byTypeKind` (a count of pins whose kind is `freeform`) but never the label text. So the import report reads the column and discards it.

Accurate statement of the finding: the cross-property freeform-label tally is computed correctly by `server/src/engine/reviewQueue.ts:69` and is reachable from no entry point — no route in `server/src/index.ts`, no script in `server/scripts/`, no npm script in either package.json, no web page. Two narrowings, neither of which kills it. (1) Individual freeform labels are not invisible: server/src/audit/binding.ts:294 sets `describedAs: pin.componentType ?? pin.freeformLabel ?? 'no type recorded'` and web/src/pages/Audit.tsx:471-473 renders them ("Evidence matching no slot … listed individually — a count cannot be chased"); server/src/import/report.ts:74,79 also SELECTs `p.freeform_label` and then never uses it in the report it builds. survivors.title: The four pass tasks each compute a "nothing was dropped" bucket into the generation record that no screen, script or route reads.
lenses: Values computed and never read — exported functions with no non-test caller, object fields populated on a write path and read on no path, and computed results discarded by the one consumer that wanted them.
survivors.why: Doctrine 6 is the stated reason each of these fields exists — resolveProduct.ts:284-291 spells out that a demoted answer is "a counted outcome" rather than a crash, and readSurfaces' `unaccounted` is a photograph that was sent, paid for, and silently not spoken about.     unaccounted: [...sent].filter((m) => !mentioned.has(m)),   // line 368

Siblings on the same write path: `unknownSurfaces`/`strayLabels` (readSurfaces.ts:146,148), `strayAnswers`/`demoted` (resolveProduct.ts:106,110), `unknownProducts`/`unknownClasses`/`strayEvidence`/`danglingParents`/`evidenceless` (matchComplete.ts:193-234), `strayEvidence`/`unevidenced` (identify.ts:171,173).

corrections:
Three corrections, one of which narrows the claim and two of which widen it.

1. THE SIBLING LIST IS WRONG ABOUT PASS 3. `matchComplete.ts`'s buckets ARE reachable. `server/scripts/match.ts:149-172` (`reportUnmodelled`) does `SELECT output FROM ai_generations WHERE ... task IN ('match_known','enumerate_room')`, then `for (const [k, v] of Object.entries(o))` skipping only `MODELLED = new Set(['located', 'couldNotLocate', 'additional', 'unsure'])`. Because `matchComplete.ts:719` stores the whole `StoredMatch`, every key it does not name — `evidenceless`, `strayEvidence`, `unknownProducts`, `unknownClasses`, `danglingParents`, `unmodelledKeys`, plus `question` and `roomNote` — is printed with a 160-char preview. So `npm run match` does surface them, though under a heading that misdescribes them ("answer key(s) this build does not model" — these are keys this build wrote itself). The grep in the evidence missed this because the reader reaches them by key-walk, not by name.

2. THE CLAIM UNDERSTATES THE PASS-1 CASE. `noText` is equally unreachable — `writeReadings` (`readSurfaces.ts:397`) stores only labels, so a photograph declared empty and a photograph nobody mentioned both leave zero rows in `readings`. `read.ts:245` prints "N labels read across M photographs" and `read.ts:134` prints "S photographs would be sent"; the gap S−M silently merges the two. The exact distinction `readSurfaces.ts:366-367` insists "must not be counted as one" is the one no reader can recover. That is a sharper statement of the defect than "the count appears nowhere".

3. PASS 2 HAS A THIRD UNLISTED BUCKET. `resolveProduct.ts:302` computes `unanswered` — "Never answered at all. **Different from `resolved: false`** — one is the model declining and the other is nobody saying anything." `server/scripts/resolve.ts:158` selects `FROM product_resolutions` and at line 208 prints "N unresolved", which is `resolved = 0` — so a query nobody answered and a query the model declined print identically. `demoted` is partially mitigated (it writes a `resolved: false` row at `resolveProduct.ts:290-291`) but is indistinguishable from an honest decline in that same report.

Accurate scope: the buckets are unreachable for `read_surfaces` (`unaccounted`, `unknownSurfaces`, `strayLabels`, `noText`), `resolve_product` (`strayAnswers`, `demoted`, `unanswered`) and `identify_objects` (`strayEvidence`, `unevidenced`, `unknownClasses` — `identify.ts:169-173`, not covered by match.ts's task filter). Pass 3 is already covered.

Narrow it from four pass tasks to three. Pass 3's residue buckets ARE reachable — accidentally — and the accident is itself worth reporting.

`server/scripts/match.ts:148-173` `reportUnmodelled()` queries `SELECT output FROM ai_generations WHERE task IN ('match_known','enumerate_room')` and prints every top-level key not in `MODELLED = new Set(['located','couldNotLocate','additional','unsure'])`. But `matchComplete.ts:719` stores `output: stored`, i.e. the whole `StoredMatch`, not the model's raw answer. I ran `normaliseMatch` and applied the script's own filter:

    stored keys: question, located, evidenceless, unmodelledKeys, couldNotLocate,
                 additional, unsure, roomNote, unknownProducts, unknownClasses,
                 strayEvidence, danglingParents
    reportUnmodelled would print:
        question: match_known
        evidenceless: ["Water heater"]
        unmodelledKeys: [{"key":"roomNote","preview":"a room"}]
        roomNote: a room
        unknownProducts: []
        unknownClasses: []
        strayEvidence: [{"label":"Water heater","mediaId":"nope"}]
        danglingParents: []

So `npm run match` does print `evidenceless`, `strayEvidence`, `unknownProducts`, `unknownClasses` and `danglingParents`. Two consequences:

(a) The finding must say readSurfaces, resolveProduct and identify — not "the four pass tasks each". The named instance at readSurfaces.ts:150 is untouched: pass 1 has no equivalent script, and `npm run read -- --report` cannot distinguish a photograph the model declared empty from one it never mentioned.

(b) The scan runs one layer too high, which damages the thing it was built for. `unmodelledKeys` is computed correctly at matchComplete.ts:447-455 against the RAW model answer; the script then recomputes against the STORED shape, so the genuine signal (`unmodelledKeys: [...]`) arrives as one line buried among eight storage keys, and `question` and `roomNote` guarantee `seen.size > 0` on every run — the `if (seen.size === 0) return` early exit at match.ts:167 can never fire. The header "⚑ N answer key(s) this build does not model. NOTHING here became an object" is then printed over `evidenceless` and `strayEvidence`, which the build models precisely. Fixing this correctly (scan `stored.unmodelledKeys` instead of re-deriving) would REMOVE the only reader the residue buckets have, so the two changes have to land together.

survivors.title: `POSITIVE_LABELS` is declared "so the scan and the reader agree" and the scan carries its own hardcoded copy instead.
lenses: Values computed and never read — exported functions with no non-test caller, object fields populated on a write path and read on no path, and computed results discarded by the one consumer that wanted them.
Capability silently dropped by a migration or refactor — a reader left pointing at nothing, or a value computed that no reader can reach.
survivors.why: The constant's stated job is to be the single place the vocabulary lives so the guard and the renderer cannot drift. With three independent copies, adding a positive label to `POSITIVE_LABELS` leaves the guard blind to it, and the guard is the thing standing between an assertion about the house and a gap row in a client's document. This is the verification note's "a check whose two sides cannot disagree" arriving from the other direction: the two sides can disagree and nothing would notice.

/**
     * Labels that assert something about the house, and therefore cannot appear on

      'observed', 'measured', 'documented', 'reported-by-homeowner', 'inferred',

`grep -rn POSITIVE_LABELS server web` → one hit, the declaration. The scan it names (server/test/doctrine.test.ts:1503-1512) duplicates the list:

      const POSITIVE = ['observed', 'measured', 'documented', 'reported-by-homeowner', 'inferred']

A third copy exists at doctrine.test.ts:714 as a regex.
corrections:
The accurate residue is narrow and not a defect: POSITIVE_LABELS is an unreferenced documentary constant, and that is consistent with rule 11b rather than a drift hazard, because the runtime funnel (names.ts:264) and the closed union (clientVoice.ts:61) — not the scan — are what actually keep a positive label off a gap row.

One genuinely separate weakness surfaced while testing, and it is NOT the claimed finding — it is about the other half of the same test. doctrine.test.ts:1518 pins the closed set with an unanchored substring match:

    assert.match(source, /export type GapLabel = 'not-accessible' \| 'not-inspected'/)

I widened the union to `export type GapLabel = 'not-accessible' | 'not-inspected' | 'certified'` and re-ran `npx tsx --test test/doctrine.test.ts`: typecheck passed and the scan reported `ok 4 - never lets a positive honesty label onto a gap row`, because the widened declaration still *contains* the pinned substring. So the assertion whose comment says "the type itself is closed" cannot observe the union being opened — only that its first two members are still there. Anyone reporting that should verify it independently; it is a different mechanism from the one this claim named, and it survives regardless of what POSITIVE_LABELS says.

The finding stands; its FALSIFIABLE AS clause is wrong in one detail and should be restated. I ran the experiment in a hardlinked copy at /tmp/.../scratchpad/repo (the working repo is being concurrently mutated by another session, so I did not test in place): appended `'certified'` to POSITIVE_LABELS, widened `GapLabel` to admit it, and changed server/src/report/clientVoice.ts:167 from `label: 'not-accessible'` to `label: 'certified'`. `npm run typecheck` passed clean, all 31 doctrine suites passed — but `npm test` reported `# fail 1`: server/test/carried-items.test.ts:288, `assert.equal(row!.label, 'not-accessible')`, "reads structured parts, not the internal sentence", failed with `actual: 'certified'`. So it is NOT true that "everything passes". What caught it was a behavioural test pinning one branch's hardcoded literal, not the guard POSITIVE_LABELS claims to serve — that test would have failed identically if the constant did not exist. The accurate statement of the defect: POSITIVE_LABELS has no reader in the repository, the doctrine scan at doctrine.test.ts:1503-1512 enforces §2b from an independent hardcoded copy, and consequently a positive label added to the constant leaves the scan blind to it — with no test anywhere comparing the two lists, or either list against `schema/binder-schema-v1.json`'s `honestyLabels`. Two secondary facts surfaced while verifying and are worth carrying with it: the type-text assertion at doctrine.test.ts:1519 is a non-anchored `assert.match`, so `GapLabel` can be widened with a positive label and that assertion still passes; and the schema's `honestyLabels` array is read by no TypeScript in the repo at all.

survivors.title: Every `record-set` slot in the binder schema is structurally incapable of producing a gap, because the four schema keys that define a record-set's expectation — `recordFields`, `completeWhen`, `expectationSource`, `keyedBy` — have zero readers anywhere in the repo.
lenses: Declared in a schema/config and consumed by nothing — every field, column, and vocabulary term in `/schema/*.json`, `server/src/db/migrations/*.sql`, and the import config snapshot, traced to a reader.
survivors.why: Five of the profile's `required` slots are record-sets: `s7.components`, `s10.findings`, `s10.concerns`, `s11.warranties`, `s13.tests` (schema/profiles/baseline-v1.json:8-40). Trace each through `assessSlot`: `s11.warranties` sources only `documents`, which has no reader, so `unwiredNote` fires and it correctly reports `empty` with its reason. The other four do not. `s10.findings` and `s13.tests` name a `field.*` source, which IS wired, so `unwiredNote` returns undefined (sources.ts:124-134), the record-set branch runs, `slot.id !== 's7.components'` yields `expected: 0`, and completeness.ts:365 turns that into **`state: 'complete'`**. `s10.concerns` declares no `sources` key at all, so `sources ?? []` is empty, `unwiredNote` returns undefined at its first guard, and it lands on the same path. `s7.components` sets `withRecord = expected` by construction, so it is `complete` when pins exist and `complete` with `expected: 0` when they do not — on a Discovery export, which migration 022 says produces zero pins by design, the house's Systems inventory reports complete. `gapList` (completeness.ts:425) filters `state !== 'complete'`, so none of the four can ever reach the gap report. The Increment 3 build spec defines the kind as "Every entity in the expectation set has a record, and each record satisfies its required fields" — neither half is implemented, and the schema keys that carry both halves have no reader. CLAUDE.md §15 records that concerns and lab results are unbuilt; the audit does not report them as unbuilt, it reports them as done. This is Verification Discipline rule 11 exactly: the only record-set that exercises the `expected` vs `withRecord` comparison is the one where the two sides are the same number.
corrections:
The finding stands. Three amendments, two of which strengthen it.

STRONGER THAN CLAIMED — the dead branches are not limited to the four slots. `withRecord` and `shortfalls` have exactly two producers, both in run.ts:473 and 480, and BOTH set `withRecord === expected` with `shortfalls: []`. So completeness.ts:369-382 — the `empty` branch and the `partial` branch of the record-set assessment — are unreachable from any real audit run. No record-set slot of any id can reach the gap list through the records path; the only record-sets that ever gap are the ones rescued by `unwiredNote` (s11.warranties, s14, s17, s20, s21). Rule 11 applies to the whole kind, not just to s7.

STRONGER THAN CLAIMED — it surfaces to a human as a section verdict, not just a slot record. Section rollups on the same reference run: s10 "Baseline condition assessment" → {"state":"complete","complete":2,...}; s13 "Testing & environmental program" → {"state":"complete","complete":1,...}. web/src/pages/Audit.tsx:165-166 renders `section.rollup.state` straight to the screen. On a two-room partial import with no concern entity implemented and no lab result in existence, the audit screen tells the operator the Baseline Condition Assessment is complete.

ONE CLAIM I COULD NOT OBSERVE — the s7.components pin-free case. I stripped top-level `pins` from the reference raw and still got `expected: 1`, because pins are not carried at the top level of that manifest. The code path plainly does what the claim says (`evidence.pins.filter((p) => !p.retired && p.componentType !== null)` → length 0 → `expected: 0` → completeness.ts:365 → complete), but that specific sentence is read from the code rather than observed, and should be stated as such.

Two corrections, neither fatal.

(1) The headline over-reaches. "Every record-set slot is structurally incapable of producing a gap" is false: s11.warranties and s17.directory are record-sets and DO appear in result.gaps (observed: state 'empty', missing "no source wired yet: this slot comes from the client's own documents / business data, which this builder does not read"). They reach the gap report through the noSourceWired short-circuit, which fires BEFORE the record-set branch. The accurate claim is narrower and is what the finder's own body argues: the record-set branch itself can never produce a gap. Every slot that actually reaches it — s7.components, s10.findings, s10.concerns, s13.tests, and s18.projects (sources ["s10.concerns"], wired because isSlotReference matches /^s\d+/) — returns 'complete'. Four of those five are `required` in baseline-v1.

(2) The finder missed a second reader, and it sharpens rather than weakens the finding. server/scripts/binder.ts:44-55 keeps a NO_PRODUCER map that names 's10.concerns': "concerns as records — §15: nothing implements them; `openConcerns` is typed `never[]`" and 's13.tests': "lab results — §15: nothing knows a result is late, or that one was ordered". So the binder-draft surface does tell a reader these are unbuilt. But it is a different surface (`npm run binder`), it reads none of the four schema keys, and its own comment concedes it is "a hand-kept list and that is a known risk in this repo — four things have drifted from a hand-kept restatement of something the data already knew." Critically it does NOT cover s10.findings, which instead gets a hardcoded zero at binder.ts:125 (`one('SELECT COUNT(*) AS n FROM audit_slots WHERE 1 = 0')`) and is absent from NO_PRODUCER — so the draft renders s10.findings as a real gap while the audit renders it complete. Two surfaces, same slot, opposite answers, and the hand-kept list exists precisely because the record-set logic cannot derive what the schema already declares.

survivors.title: `neverAI` and `aiMayDraft` — doctrine 9's "Never AI" list, written into the binder schema as machine-readable flags on six slots and fields — have no reader anywhere in the repository.
lenses: Declared in a schema/config and consumed by nothing — every field, column, and vocabulary term in `/schema/*.json`, `server/src/db/migrations/*.sql`, and the import config snapshot, traced to a reader.
survivors.why: This is the failure `server/src/report/renderGate.ts:19-24` names in its own header and then does not generalise: *"The obvious build is a `renderNote` on the slot that a renderer may emit. **That is Table I** — `audit/provenance.ts`, five exported functions built, tested, and called by nothing... An optional field is satisfied by declaring it; the failure it exists to prevent survives untouched."* `neverAI` is that shape precisely. The `requiresHumanAccept` half happens to be covered by accident — `ai/accept.ts` makes human acceptance universal for every generation, so nameplate fields cannot bypass a signature whether or not the flag is read. There is no equivalent universal mechanism for `neverAI`: nothing anywhere refuses to route `s19.reserve-figure`, `urgency`, `planning-cost-range`, `recommended-action`, `planning-horizon` or `replacement-allowance` to a model. Today the consequence is latent rather than active — no binder-section renderer exists and no AI task writes into an s7 record field or an s10 concern field, so no value can currently reach one of these. But `docs/…Property-Flags-and-Session-Plan_Code-Reply_2026-08-07.md:136` already describes a render check that treats `neverAI` and `classD_irreduciblyHuman` as hard refusals, and neither key is read. The wall is written down where a future author will read it as already enforced.

corrections:
The finding stands as written, with two qualifications that narrow its framing (neither kills it), plus one sharpening.

QUALIFICATION 1 — 'unread schema key' is the schema's ordinary state, so 'no reader' alone is not the defect. I enumerated all 36 slot-level keys in binder-schema-v1.json: roughly 20 have no code reader (bindsTo, bindingRule, completeWhen, dependsOn, expectationRule, expectedComponents, inFlightRule, itemRule, itemStates, itemsFrom, keyedBy, lateResults, neverGaps, recordFields, removedField, sessionAttestation, specificityRule, zoneIndependence, aiMayDraft, neverAI). The schema's own top-level `note` frames the file as a Master-Spec transcription that runs ahead of code ('Coarse first… Content passes continue'), and CLAUDE.md §4.8 says the software does not invent what a binder contains. So the argument must be sharper than 'unread': the defect is that a machine-shaped PROHIBITION is declared, is described in a design doc as producing a hard render refusal, and is nowhere labelled as not-yet-enforced — which is exactly CLAUDE.md §15's own rule ('what was a defect is that only one of them said so').

QUALIFICATION 2 — the classD comparison cuts the other way and is worth stating. `classD_irreduciblyHuman` at schema/profiles/baseline-v1.json:57 is also unread, but it is not machine-addressable at all: its members are ["s2.top-items ordering", "s19.reserve-figure", "client conversation and handover"] — two of the three are not slot ids. That is what a human-planning declaration looks like. `neverAI: true` on a slot and `neverAI: ["urgency","planning-cost-range","recommended-action"]` on s10's recordFields are addressable and machine-shaped, which is why they read as a gate rather than as prose.

SHARPENING — the honest limit is correctly stated but can be made concrete: the value CAN already cross today, it just has nowhere to go. `gate()` accepts any string from any caller and I demonstrated it clearing an explicitly AI-labelled reserve figure. The absent piece is a renderer downstream, not a guard upstream. That matters because renderGate.ts:71-76 argues for exactly this ordering — 'the guard has to be in place before the temptation' — so the module that names the failure built its own guard ahead of Increment 6 and left the neverAI half of the same slot unguarded.

The requiresHumanAccept half should be dropped from the headline or explicitly demoted; the claim already concedes accept.ts makes acceptance universal, and including four line numbers for a flag that is covered by accident dilutes the six that are not.

One narrower observation survives and is worth a sentence rather than a finding: on a single slot, schema/binder-schema-v1.json:1118-1119, `s19.reserve-figure` declares "neverAI": true and "outsideHonestyVocabulary" adjacently, and only the second has a guard built ahead of its consumer. renderGate.ts's own header argues for exactly that discipline — "the guard has to be in place before the temptation" — so if a neverAI enforcement point is ever wanted, the precedent for building it before Increment 6 sits on the neighbouring line. That is a design note, not a defect: no AI task writes into an s7 record field, an s10 concern field or s19 today, accept.ts requires a human actor for every value that becomes state, and no binder-section renderer exists to emit one.

survivors.title: The `object_states` table and every function that gives its vocabulary consequence — `suppressesCare`, `blocksOperation`, `doNotOperateLine` — have no production writer and no production reader; only tests touch either.
lenses: Declared in a schema/config and consumed by nothing — every field, column, and vocabulary term in `/schema/*.json`, `server/src/db/migrations/*.sql`, and the import config snapshot, traced to a reader.
