The accurate finding is the read side alone: objects.resolution_id has no production reader, and the consumer built to use it is called blind. server/src/engine/compare.ts:171 takes `bindings: readonly Binding[] = []` where `Binding {objectId, productKey}` is documented (compare.ts:87-89) as "an object tied to a resolved product — Amendment 11 pass 2's output"; server/scripts/compare.ts:125 calls `compareProposals(proposals)` with the comment "Bindings come from Amendment 11 pass 2, which is unbuilt", and pass 2 has been built since 2026-08-12 (resolveProduct.ts:1; commit 1a32956) — a day before both compare files were last edited. proposalsForImport (compare.ts:328) selects derived_from, model_read and generation_id and omits resolution_id, so the binding cannot be assembled. Consequence: comparison stage 1 reports "bound to a product 0" and states the PRE-binding reason (compare.ts:230-233), the derived-same / derived-different halves have never run on data that exists, and compare.test.ts:70-77 asserts the stale sentence as a requirement. The fix is one join — `SELECT o.id, p.product FROM objects o JOIN product_resolutions p ON p.id = o.resolution_id` — plus deleting the "unbuilt" note and its test. The migration's word "checkable" then becomes true, and a plate row with a NULL resolution would show up as unbound instead of being indistinguishable.

survivors.title: `ai_generations.confidence` has a reader that survived with no writer — nine `recordGeneration` call sites and not one passes the field, so `Proposal.confidence` is structurally always null.
lenses: Capability silently dropped by a migration or refactor — a reader left pointing at nothing, or a value computed that no reader can reach.
survivors.why: The column is the only numeric confidence field in the schema and it is dead: `SELECT confidence FROM ai_generations` returns NULL for every row the system has ever written. Anyone reasoning about the AI ledger — cost, accuracy, which proposals were weak — will find the column, find `Proposal.confidence` reading it, and conclude a per-generation confidence exists. It does not; confidence moved to the per-candidate arrays inside `output` when routing and pin-typing were built, and the top-level reader was left in place. Nothing renders it today, so the consequence is a false affordance rather than a wrong number on a screen — but it is a null that reads as "no confidence" rather than "never measured", the exact merge this repo refuses elsewhere (models.ts:151-157 goes out of its way to keep a cost of zero and an unknown cost apart).
survivors.evidence:
The reader:

    server/src/ai/accept.ts:365   confidence: number | null            (on `interface Proposal`)
    server/src/ai/accept.ts:388   confidence: g.confidence,            (in `toProposal`)

The writer, with the field optional:

    server/src/ai/queue.ts:374    confidence?: number | null
    server/src/ai/queue.ts:399    args.abstained ? 1 : 0, args.confidence ?? null,

Every call site — worker.ts:199, nameplate.ts:166, nameplate.ts:243, identify.ts:629, matchComplete.ts:690, pinType.ts:298, readSurfaces.ts:501, routing.ts:364, resolveProduct.ts:405 — and none of them names it:

    grep -rn --include=*.ts 'confidence:' server/src | grep -v test
      server/src/ai/tasks/pinType.ts:56,109,341     ← per-candidate, inside the output JSON
      server/src/ai/tasks/routing.ts:96,119,162,412 ← per-candidate, inside the output JSON
      server/src/ai/accept.ts:39,365,388            ← the orphaned reader

The live confidence signal lives per candidate in the stored `output` blob and is typed as a word, not a number (`server/src/ai/confidence.ts`), which is what `web/src/pass/Assist.tsx:752,849,864` renders.
corrections: The accurate, non-defect version: `ai_generations.confidence` is a spec-mandated nullable column (Increment-1 Build-Spec v3.4:109; migration 001_initial.sql:352) that is deliberately never written, because server/src/ai/confidence.ts:1-19 rules that confidence in this system is three words (`certain`/`likely`/`possible`), not a number — "a model asked for 0.87 will produce 0.87, and it will mean nothing." The live signal therefore lives per candidate inside the stored `output` blob, which is what web/src/pass/Assist.tsx:752,849,864 renders. `Proposal.confidence` (server/src/ai/accept.ts:365,388) is a vestigial pass-through of that never-written column with zero consumers — verified by removing it and typechecking clean. The only defensible action is a one-line comment on accept.ts:365 saying the column is deliberately never populated, so a future reader does not mistake NULL for a measurement. Do not remove the column: the spec mandates it and calls it nullable.

Two refinements, neither of which weakens it.

First, "a reader that survived with no writer" is precise but the shape is three artifacts, not two: the column (`server/src/db/migrations/001_initial.sql:352` — `confidence REAL,`), an unfilled parameter (`server/src/ai/queue.ts:374,399` — optional, defaulted, never passed), and the reader (`server/src/ai/accept.ts:39,365,388`). `queue.ts` is not a writer that stopped writing; it is a parameter that was never once supplied. The finding's own falsification test is the right one and it passes: making the field required breaks all fourteen call sites, deleting it breaks only `queue.ts:399`'s own `args.confidence ?? null`.

Second, "nothing renders it today" is right about rendering but the null does reach the browser. `discardProposal` returns `findGeneration(db, generationId)!` (`accept.ts:297`), which is `SELECT * FROM ai_generations` (`accept.ts:46`), and `server/src/index.ts:711` does `res.json(discardProposal(db, gen.id, {...}))`. So every discard response body carries `"confidence": null` over the wire, where `web/src/api.ts:767` types it `req<unknown>` and drops it. That makes the false affordance slightly wider than stated — it is visible in the API surface, not only in the schema — while confirming the consequence is a misleading null rather than a wrong value on a screen.

survivors.title: The binder draft's Findings count reads `audit_slots WHERE 1 = 0` — a predicate that can never return a row — while the findings the import actually recorded sit in `resolutions.records_finding`.
lenses: The write path and the read path disagree — who INSERTs vs who SELECTs, per table in server/src/db/migrations
The write path and the read path disagree — who INSERTs vs who SELECTs, per table in server/src/db/migrations
checks whose output does not depend on what they check
Client-facing overclaim — every rendered sentence held against the provenance behind it, across `server/src/report/**`, `server/scripts/binder.ts`, and the House Style lint that gates them.

Free sweep — first-tour reading of server/src, server/scripts, schema/, prompts/ and web/src, plus a real end-to-end run of the pipeline (import the walk fixture → audit → gap-report draft → signed edition → binder draft) to compare what the code computes against what a reader actually receives.
survivors.why: binderDraft.ts's whole stated purpose is that "the measure of a good draft is not how full it is — it is whether a reviewer can tell a missing producer from a missing fact." This one slot is guaranteed to tell the reviewer the opposite of the truth: it prints "the visit did not supply it" over a visit that supplied four findings, and s10.findings is counted in the run's `gaps` total rather than `filled`. The outside review this document is spending is misdirected onto a hole that is not one, and section 10 — Findings, the condition-assessment stream CLAUDE.md §5 calls the most damaging thing to collapse — is the section it is wrong about.
survivors.evidence:
server/scripts/binder.ts:125
  ['s10.findings', one('SELECT COUNT(*) AS n FROM audit_slots WHERE 1 = 0')],

The writer that produces findings is server/src/import/persist.ts:307
  const recordsFinding = (r.kind === 'na' && reason?.recordsFinding === true) || r.result === 'fail'
and the working reader is server/src/import/report.ts:185-186
  `SELECT item_id, kind, result, reason_id, scope_kind FROM resolutions
   WHERE import_id = ? AND records_finding = 1 ORDER BY item_id`

Run against fixtures/reference (npx tsx, in-memory db, real runImport):
  resolutions with records_finding=1 : 4
  binder.ts's s10.findings count     : 0

Feeding that 0 through buildDraft with the real schema + baseline profile gives the slot a reviewer reads:
  { "id": "s10.findings", "expectation": "required", "count": 0, "filled": false,
    "emptyReason": "not-captured",
    "says": "**GAP — this ought to be here and is not.** The producer exists and the visit did not supply it." }

No comment anywhere defends `WHERE 1 = 0`; `git log -S` shows it entering unremarked in 70fb147, and the commit message does not mention it.
corrections:
The claim is accurate as stated. Two points of added precision worth carrying into the report:

(a) The numbers: reference = 4 findings (2 `result='fail'` + 2 `na` with `recordsFinding`), walk-2026-07-31 = 2 (both fails). So the mislabel fires on both fixtures in the repo, not just one.

(b) The fix is not simply "point the query at resolutions". Two honest outcomes exist and the current code is neither: either count `resolutions WHERE records_finding = 1` — in which case CLAUDE.md §5 forbids rendering the total alone under a heading that implies trouble, since `says` would print "4 entries" over 2 defects and 2 confirmed absences, so the breakdown has to travel — or declare s10.findings in NO_PRODUCER with its reason, which renders "nothing in the builder can fill this yet". What is indefensible is the third thing it does today: a constant zero rendered to an outside reviewer as "the producer exists and the visit did not supply it", over a visit that supplied four.

None to the substance; two refinements. (1) `audit_slots` is not an absurd table to have reached for — server/src/audit/run.ts:356 writes one row per binder slot per audit run, so a row keyed `slot_id = 's10.findings'` does exist after an audit and carries a state. That makes line 125 look like a query someone started and never finished rather than a deliberate placeholder; `WHERE 1 = 0` reads none of it either way. (2) There is a defensible argument that the right fix is NOT to count resolutions — a binder Findings record is Class C (AI drafts, human signs), and four raw checklist answers are evidence, not authored records. But that argument lands on NO_PRODUCER: the slot would then render `no-producer` ("nothing in the builder can fill this yet"). It does not rescue today's output, which renders `not-captured` ("the producer exists and the visit did not supply it") over a visit that supplied four findings. Note also that schema/binder-schema-v1.json:832 declares s10.findings' sources as `field.check:fail` and `field.na:recordsFinding` — precisely the two conditions server/src/import/persist.ts:307 ORs together to set `records_finding` — so the finder's mapping is the schema's own, not an invention.

survivors.title: A gap-report row whose column edit names an unknown column id disappears from every column, from `withheld`, and from the signed edition, and nothing counts it.
lenses: doctrine 6 — never drop anything silently
survivors.why: The gap report is the one-page artifact a homeowner receives, and a signed edition is a dated snapshot the binder stands on. A row that a concierge deliberately moved leaves the document with no trace: `withheld` — the mechanism built precisely so "a withheld row nobody hears about is a dropped row with extra steps" cannot happen — stays empty, the `render.nothing-included` guard still sees 20 included rows, the House Style lint never sees the sentence, and neither the desk screen (GapReport.tsx:148 re-filters `draft.rows` by column the same way) nor the edition record reports 19 of 20. The row is not withheld, not excluded, and not rendered — it is gone, while every counter says the report is complete.
survivors.evidence:
draft.ts:183  `else if (row.kind === 'column') edits.column = payload.column as ColumnId`   — a bare cast, no validation
draft.ts:263  `column: edit?.column ?? (item.column_id as ColumnId),`
draft.ts:328  `columns: COLUMNS.map((c) => ({ ...c, rows: rows.filter((r) => r.column === c.id && r.included) })),`
render.ts:157 `const included = draft.rows.filter((r) => r.included)`
render.ts:169 `const rows = included.filter((r) => r.column === column.id)`
index.ts:783  validates `kind` against the five edit kinds — and index.ts:797 then passes `payload: req.body ?? {}` through untouched, so `column` is never checked. index.ts:819 has the same hole for a typed row: `column: (req.body?.column as ColumnId) ?? 'missing-from-you'`.

Run against the reference import (probe, since deleted):
  before  totals : rows 20 in columns 20 withheld 0
  writeEdit(..., kind: 'column', payload: { column: 'missing-from-them' })
  after   column : missing-from-them  because: moved here by hand  included: true
  after   in a column : false
  after   in withheld : false
  after   totals : rows 20 in columns 19 withheld 0

And through `signEdition`:
  rendered edition columns rows: [ 0, 19, 0 ]
  edition.withheld            : []
  HTML mentions the row name  : false  ( "Outside exhaust vents" )
corrections: Two accuracy notes that narrow who can trigger it today without weakening the finding. First, there is no UI control anywhere that issues a `column` edit: grep finds 'column' as an edit kind only at index.ts:785, draft.ts:183 and the EditKind union — zero callers in /web, zero tests. So today the silent drop is reachable only by a hand-made HTTP request to POST /api/properties/:id/report/rows/:rowKey/column, or via the manual-row route at index.ts:819 (`column: (req.body?.column as ColumnId) ?? 'missing-from-you'`) with a bad `column` in the body, which the shipped UI never sends because GapReport.tsx passes `id` from draft.columns. The missing guard therefore sits exactly where the future move-a-row control will connect. Second, an edit whose payload omits `column` entirely is a harmless no-op — `edits.column` stays undefined and draft.ts:263 falls back to `item.column_id`; only a present-but-unknown value drops the row. The claim's framing "a row that a concierge deliberately moved" should read "a column edit carrying an unrecognised column id, from any caller".

The mechanism and observed behaviour are exactly as claimed. Three scopings should ride with it. (1) NOT REACHABLE FROM THE DESK TODAY: the web front end never emits a `column` edit — `web/src/pages/GapReport.tsx` calls `api.editReportRow` only with `'exclude'`/`'include'` (line 361) and `'reword'` (line 297); there is no move-column control anywhere in `web/src`, and no test writes one. So "a row a concierge deliberately moved" overstates the trigger: today only a direct HTTP caller can reach `POST /api/properties/:id/report/rows/:rowKey/column`. That the affordance is allow-listed at `server/src/index.ts:785` and documented in `013_report_editor.sql:71` ("For `column`, the column moved to") keeps it a supported path with no producer, not a defect that cannot fire. (2) "NO TRACE" IS TRUE OF THE DOCUMENT, NOT OF THE API: the row is still in the `rows` array of `GET /api/properties/:id/report` carrying `column: 'missing-from-them'`, and `rowTrail` still shows the edit. What loses it is every rendering path — the three desk columns, the signed HTML, and `edition.withheld`. And it is worse than "nothing counts it": `GapReport.tsx:81` counts it as present, so the header reads "20 row(s) in" while the three columns render 19 — the desk actively asserts completeness. (3) THE UNDERLYING GAP IS NOT LOST FROM THE SYSTEM: `audit_carried_items` is untouched, and `server/src/plan/sessionPlan.ts:443` recomputes `carriedGaps` from evidence via `carriedItems({ evidence, active, resolutions })` rather than from the draft, so the item still carries to the next visit. The loss is confined to the client-facing artifact and the desk screen — where it matters most, but narrower than "gone".

survivors.title: `normaliseMatch`'s MODELLED set omits `roomNote`, which MATCH_SCHEMA makes required — so the un-modelled-key channel fires falsely on every real call and, because the schema forbids extra properties, can never fire truly.
lenses: doctrine 6 — never drop anything silently
survivors.why: `StoredMatch.unmodelledKeys` is documented as "where a hypothesis lands first" and as the specification for an unbuilt channel — so the content of this bucket is meant to be read as evidence about what the model wanted to say. It contains one entry, `roomNote`, on every call, and cannot contain anything else: the output schema is strict, so the set of possible top-level keys is exactly the five in `required`. The bucket therefore carries no information at all, while the field it names is simultaneously stored and used. Nothing links MODELLED to `MatchOutput`'s keys, so typecheck cannot notice, and the two copies of the list (here and match.ts:157) can drift independently.
survivors.evidence:
matchComplete.ts:88   `required: ['located', 'couldNotLocate', 'additional', 'unsure', 'roomNote'],`  (with `additionalProperties: false` at :87)
matchComplete.ts:448  `const MODELLED = new Set(['located', 'couldNotLocate', 'additional', 'unsure'])`
matchComplete.ts:531  `roomNote: typeof output.roomNote === 'string' ? output.roomNote : '',`   — it *is* modelled, and stored

Probe on one schema-valid answer (since deleted):
  schema required : [ 'located', 'couldNotLocate', 'additional', 'unsure', 'roomNote' ]
  additionalProps : false
  unmodelledKeys  : [{"key":"roomNote","preview":"the utility room is tight; two frames are of the same wall"}]
  roomNote stored : "the utility room is tight; two frames are of the same wall"

The negative test that is supposed to make the check falsifiable uses an input the API cannot return — match-complete.test.ts:429 asserts `unmodelledKeys` is `[]` for `{ located: [], couldNotLocate: [], additional: [], unsure: [] }`, an object missing the required `roomNote`. Its comment reads: "The half that lets the check fail: a reporter that always fires is noise." It always fires.
corrections:
Two refinements, both strengthening rather than softening.

1. Precision on the claim: the bucket is not merely "carries no information" — it is a constant. On every real call it is exactly `[{ key: 'roomNote', preview: <the note> }]`, never more and never less, because matchComplete.ts:87 `additionalProperties: false` is enforced by the structured-output request at client.ts:170.

2. THE SAME BUG HAS A SECOND, WORSE INSTANCE — the reader end, which is the half that actually matters. server/scripts/match.ts:157 carries the identical four-key set:
      const MODELLED = new Set(['located', 'couldNotLocate', 'additional', 'unsure'])
but it diffs it against the WRONG OBJECT. It reads `SELECT output FROM ai_generations` (match.ts:152-158), and matchComplete.ts:719 records `output: stored` — queue.ts:398 `JSON.stringify(args.output ?? null)` — so the column holds a `StoredMatch`, never the model's raw answer. The raw answer is not persisted anywhere.

StoredMatch's twelve top-level keys are, verified by probe: question, located, evidenceless, unmodelledKeys, couldNotLocate, additional, unsure, roomNote, unknownProducts, unknownClasses, strayEvidence, danglingParents. Subtract the same four and `npm run match` prints eight of the builder's own bookkeeping fields — question, evidenceless, unmodelledKeys, roomNote, unknownProducts, unknownClasses, strayEvidence, danglingParents — under the banner at match.ts:167:
      `\n⚑ ${seen.size} answer key(s) this build does not model. NOTHING here became an object:`
followed by "These are where a hypothesis lands first". Its own header comment (match.ts:139-148) claims "Whatever turns up in this list is what the model wanted to say and had nowhere to put." It cannot be: the model's words are not in that column. The one surface a human reads this channel on is guaranteed to print eight false entries and structurally incapable of ever printing a true one.

That makes this a clean instance of the signature class at both ends — the value is computed (correctly, minus roomNote) and the reader's path to it reaches a different object entirely.

The fix is three edits, not one: add `'roomNote'` to the set at matchComplete.ts:448; derive it from the `MatchOutput` keys so typecheck notices next time a field is added (e.g. a `const MATCH_KEYS = ['located','couldNotLocate','additional','unsure','roomNote'] as const satisfies readonly (keyof MatchOutput)[]`, shared with match.ts); and either persist the raw answer alongside `stored` or have match.ts read `unmodelledKeys` off the stored record instead of re-deriving it. The negative test at match-complete.test.ts:430 then needs an input the API can actually return — all five required keys — or it goes on testing an impossible shape.

The finding stands, but two details in it should be sharpened — and the second makes it materially worse, not smaller.

**(a) "simultaneously stored and used" overstates the second half.** `roomNote` is stored — `runMatchComplete` passes `output: stored` to `recordGeneration` (`matchComplete.ts:684`, `server/src/ai/queue.ts:398` `JSON.stringify(args.output ?? null)`), so it lands in `ai_generations.output`. But nothing ever reads it back. It is modelled, typed, prompted for and persisted; it is not consumed. The contradiction is still real (a key with a schema property, a type field, a normalisation branch and its own prompt section is by any definition modelled), it is just "modelled and stored" rather than "modelled and used".

**(b) The second copy at `server/scripts/match.ts:157` is not merely a drift risk — it is already wrong, and worse, because it is applied to the wrong object.** `reportUnmodelled()` (`server/scripts/match.ts:148-172`) reads `SELECT output FROM ai_generations`, but that column holds the *normalised* `StoredMatch`, not the raw model answer. `StoredMatch` has twelve top-level keys. Filtering the same four MODELLED names off it leaves eight. I simulated the exact loop on a representative `StoredMatch`:

    8 keys reported:
        question: match_known
        evidenceless: []
        unmodelledKeys: [{"key":"roomNote","preview":"x"}]
        roomNote: tight utility room
        unknownProducts: []
        unknownClasses: []
        strayEvidence: []
        danglingParents: []

So `npm run match` (wired in `package.json`) prints, on every run:

    ⚑ 8 answer key(s) this build does not model. NOTHING here became an object:

listing the builder's *own* normalisation fields — including `unmodelledKeys` itself, and including `strayEvidence` and `danglingParents`, which are dedicated reporting buckets this same file goes on to describe as deliberate. This is the human-facing end of the channel the header at `match.ts:138-147` calls "where a hypothesis lands first" and "the hypothesis channel's specification writing itself." It carries zero signal in both places: the in-memory bucket always holds exactly `roomNote` and nothing else, and the printed report always holds the same eight builder-internal field names. The failure shape is exactly the one being hunted — the value is computed, and the reader cannot reach anything true through it.

survivors.title: `declarationOf` returns the same `{ tier: 'standard', text: null }` for four different states, one of which is "the config never declared this item" — and the caller stamps `certain: true, unrecognised: []` beside it.
lenses: doctrine 6 — never drop anything silently
survivors.why: This is the v4 path — "v4 ships the field's own resolved set and this module reads it" (activeItems.ts:15) — i.e. the production path, and the failure it exists to prevent is named in the same header: "two apps disagreeing about whether an item was ever due, with nothing to error." An item id the field ships that this import's config does not declare is exactly that divergence, and it arrives as an ordinary standard-tier item whose record positively claims `certain: true` and `unrecognised: []`, with no warning on the set and no line on the import report. Doctrine 7 requires unknown item ids to be preserved, displayed, counted and marked unrecognised; three of the four are missing. It is also the third state the Verification-Discipline note's rule 6 asks for — declared-standard vs never-declared — collapsed into the reassuring one.
corrections:
The finding survives but must be restated smaller and in a different place.

STRIKE the `certain: true, unrecognised: []` half — it is a category error, not a false assertion. Both fields carry trigger-gate semantics, not declaredness: `activeItems.ts:89` documents `certain` as "False when a fail-open decision put it here", `carriedItems.ts:93` repeats it, `triggers.ts:341` defines `unrecognised` as "Every id the vocabulary did not declare" where the ids are gate refs (`property.solar`, `zone.finished`) populated by `lookup()` at `triggers.ts:508-531`, and `web/src/pages/Audit.tsx:303-304` renders it as "applies only because {refs} is undeclared". On a received set no gate is evaluated, so `certain: true` truthfully says "no fail-open decision put this here" and `unrecognised: []` truthfully says "no gate ref went unrecognised". Writing an item id into that array would print a false sentence in the Audit UI. Nothing "positively claims" anything — `certain: true` merely suppresses an extra span.

CORRECT "three of the four are missing" to one of four. Preserve: the row is stored verbatim (`persist.ts:342-352`) and survives into the set under its own id. Display: if unresolved it reaches the desk gap list with the raw id in `parts.what` — `carriedItems.ts:283` composes `${item.itemId} in ${item.where}`, rendered at `Audit.tsx:293`. Count: it is in `origins.received` and in the "N of M applicable item(s)" denominator (`carriedItems.ts:150-160`). Only "mark unrecognised" is absent. Membership is unaffected, unlike the undeclared-na-reason case at `vocabulary.ts:167-181` where the miss changes which stream an item lands in — which is why that one got a warning and is a fair reason this one is less severe than stated.

MOVE the defect off `declarationOf`. That function is documented as "One item's tier and text, from the import's own config snapshot" (`activeItems.ts:292`) — a value lookup whose return type `{tier, text}` has no slot for a third state, and `'standard'` is the repo-wide default tier used identically at `activeItems.ts:354` and `zoneAudit.ts:209`. It answers what it is asked, honestly. The two actual holes are (a) `checkVocabulary` never reads `c.activeItems[].itemId` though it is version-agnostic and already reads the other two bearers, and (b) `fromReceived` (`activeItems.ts:260-289`) surfaces scope divergence in words and item-id divergence not at all — the tier collapses to `standard` and renders as "standard" at `Audit.tsx:293`, indistinguishable from a declared standard item, which is Verification-Discipline rule 6's exact shape.

CORRECT the reachability caveat. The claim says "no fixture can currently exercise it" and implies the path is dormant. `fromReceived` is exercised by six tests today through the injection seam, and `server/test/active-item-set.test.ts:17-27` states that the absent v4 adapter "is a decision rather than an omission" and that "A v4 adapter that fills that array is then the only new code". The path is live in test and gated only on a v3 manifest's `activeItems: []` (`adapters/v3.ts:294`). Adding the `checkVocabulary` arm would be a no-op on every current fixture — worth stating, because a check whose input is always empty is itself the shape Verification-Discipline rule 7 warns about, so it would need negative-testing against an injected undeclared id rather than being counted as covered.

Three parts of the claim are overstated and should be restated before the finding is used. 1. "The caller asserts the opposite" is wrong about `certain: true, unrecognised: []`. Those fields have a narrower documented meaning than the finder gives them — activeItems.ts:89 "False when a fail-open decision put it here", and triggers.ts:404 `certain: value !== 'unknown'` — they describe whether an *undeclared trigger fact ref* gated the item in, not whether the item id is known. web/src/pages/Audit.tsx:304 confirms it: `!item.certain` renders "applies only because {unrecognised} is undeclared". The same pair is hardcoded `certain: true, unrecognised: []` at server/src/report/render.ts:283-284 and server/src/report/draft.ts:250 for rows reconstructed from storage, so it is a shape-filling convention on non-trigger paths, not a positive claim. The defect is the *absence* of any channel that says "this id is undeclared", not a false statement in these two fields. 2. "Three of the four are missing" from doctrine 7 (preserve, display, count, mark unrecognised) is wrong; one is missing. The id is preserved verbatim in `active_items` and in `audit_carried_items`, counted in `origins.received` and `carried.byScope`, and displayed — web/src/pages/Audit.tsx:291 renders `{item.itemId}`. Only "mark unrecognised" is absent. The accurate charge is that it is displayed *indistinguishably from a declared item*, which is rule 6, not a doctrine-7 drop. 3. The `tier` half is nearly inert and should not lead. `tier` is not a column of `audit_carried_items` (run.ts:378-393), and both render paths re-fabricate it — server/src/report/render.ts:271 and server/src/report/draft.ts:250 both hardcode `tier: 'standard'`. Its only live consumer is Audit.tsx:293. So the wrong tier changes one desk badge; the load-bearing part is that no warning exists on the set, the stream, or the import report. Accurate statement: `declarationOf` (server/src/audit/activeItems.ts:293-309) collapses "never declared" into the same `{ tier: 'standard', text: null }` it returns for "declared with no tier", so no caller can distinguish them; `fromReceived` therefore admits a field-shipped item id this import's config does not declare as an ordinary standard-tier gap row, while making the unknown-zone and unknown-pin cases visible in words eleven lines below; and `checkVocabulary` never inspects `activeItems`, so the divergence the module's own header exists to prevent ("two apps disagreeing about whether an item was ever due, with nothing to error", activeItems.ts:11-12) arrives with nothing to error. Latent until a v4 adapter fills `canonical.activeItems`.

survivors.title: Twelve anomaly buckets across the four AI task normalisers are computed, documented as "reported, never dropped", and read by nothing outside the module that writes them.
lenses: doctrine 6 — never drop anything silently
survivors.why: The repo states the applicable standard itself, in match.ts:141: *"a bucket that is reported into a variable nobody prints is the same drop one layer up."* That standard was applied to exactly one of thirteen buckets, and the one printer it produced reads the wrong object (see the `reportUnmodelled` finding). The sharpest instance is `unaccounted`: a photograph pass 1 sent to the model and got no answer about at all — neither a label nor a `noText` declaration. Its own comment says it "must not be counted as" no-text, because that is a hole rather than a result. Today the distinction is drawn correctly in memory and then dissolved: downstream, both look identical, because nothing reads the field. `evidenceless` has a documented, paid-for instance behind it ("Pressurized bladder tank isolation hardware ... became the run's only false positive") — the object is refused, and the refusal is announced to nobody.
survivors.evidence:
readSurfaces.ts:364-368:
```
    // A photograph the model neither read nor declared empty. **Not the same as
    // "no text" and it must not be counted as one** — nobody said anything about
    // it, which is a hole rather than a result.
    unaccounted: [...sent].filter((m) => !mentioned.has(m)),
```
The module header at readSurfaces.ts:310-316 says: "Turn one answer into something storable. **Nothing is discarded.** ... each is kept and reported. Doctrine 6."

Reader count outside `server/src/ai/tasks/` (grep over server/src, web/src, server/scripts for each name; the two `unaccounted` hits are prose in engine/score.ts comments, and every `unanswered` hit is an unrelated identifier in audit/ and plan/):
  strayEvidence 0 · unknownClasses 0 · unevidenced 0 · unknownSurfaces 0 · strayLabels 0
  unaccounted 0 · demoted 0 · strayAnswers 0 · evidenceless 0 · danglingParents 0
  unknownProducts 0 · unmodelledKeys 0

Other instances with the same doc-comment/no-reader pattern:
  identify.ts:520      `unevidenced,`        header at :464 — "**Nothing is discarded.** ... each is kept, corrected where correction is honest, and reported. Doctrine 6"
  resolveProduct.ts:304 `demoted,`           header at :259 — "**Nothing is discarded.**"
  matchComplete.ts:521-524  `evidenceless`, `strayEvidence`, `danglingParents`, `unknownProducts`, `unknownClasses`

All thirteen live only inside the `ai_generations.output` JSON blob (queue.ts:398). No script prints them (`grep -n "stray|dangling|evidenceless|unknownProduct|unknownClass" server/scripts/*.ts` → nothing), no API route returns them, and `buildAssists` (ai/screen.ts:163) handles only EXTRACT_TASK and PIN_TYPE_TASK, so pass-1/2/3 proposals never reach a screen.
corrections:
Six, not twelve, and the sharpest example is wrong.

Accurate claim: six anomaly-bucket names across THREE normalisers — identify.ts (`unevidenced`, plus its own `unknownClasses`/`strayEvidence` values, which match.ts:153's `task IN ('match_known','enumerate_room')` filter excludes), readSurfaces.ts (`unknownSurfaces`, `strayLabels`, `unaccounted`), resolveProduct.ts (`strayAnswers`, `demoted`) — are computed, documented "Nothing is discarded", and have no reader anywhere: no script, no route, no screen. Reaching them requires hand-querying `ai_generations.output` in SQLite.

The matchComplete six (`evidenceless`, `strayEvidence`, `unknownClasses`, `unknownProducts`, `danglingParents`, `unmodelledKeys`) must be struck from the finding. They ARE printed, by match.ts:149-176. Drop the `evidenceless` / "Pressurized bladder tank isolation hardware" evidence entirely — that refusal is announced.

Two caveats worth carrying into the separate `reportUnmodelled` finding rather than this one: match.ts:163's `seen.has(k)` short-circuit means only the NEWEST of the last 20 generations contributes a value for each key, so on a multi-room run the other rooms' `evidenceless`/`strayEvidence` values are still invisible; and match.ts:164 truncates each to 160 chars. That makes the matchComplete path a degraded reader, not a working one — but a reader, which is what this finding asserted did not exist.

Lead with `unaccounted` (readSurfaces.ts:368). It is the only instance where the module writes a comment insisting on a distinction ("must not be counted as [no text]") that no reader can observe, because writeReadings persists `labels` alone.

The scope is half what was claimed, and the mechanism is the opposite of "no printer exists."

Accurate version: **Six of the twelve buckets — `unknownSurfaces`, `strayLabels`, `unaccounted` (readSurfaces.ts:363-368), `unevidenced` (identify.ts:520), `strayAnswers` and `demoted` (resolveProduct.ts:300-304) — reach no reader.** The other six live on `StoredMatch` and are printed in full by `reportUnmodelled()` at server/scripts/match.ts:150-175, because that function reads the stored normalised object rather than the raw answer and skips only `located/couldNotLocate/additional/unsure`.

Two consequences the original claim inverts:

1. The `evidenceless` example is the wrong exhibit — it is the one bucket demonstrably printed, with the bladder-tank string on screen. The surviving exhibit is `unaccounted` (readSurfaces.ts:368): `noText` is never written to a table either, so a photograph the model declared empty and one it never mentioned are identical in `report()`'s output, which is exactly what the comment at :364-366 forbids.

2. `reportUnmodelled` reading the stored object is not only the bug the finder filed separately — it is also the accidental reason match's buckets are reachable at all. Fixing that bug to read the raw answer (as its comment at :139-141 intends) would silently remove the only reader those six buckets have, converting six live values into six dead ones. Any fix must add explicit printing of the `StoredMatch` buckets at the same time.

Also worth noting against the claim's "no path" framing: `server/scripts/passes.ts` — the all-three-passes runner — never calls `reportUnmodelled()`, so the six reachable buckets are visible via `npm run match` but not via `npm run passes`. That is a narrower, checkable defect than the one claimed.

survivors.title: The personal-data scan never reads `modelRead`, the field that carries most of the plate text it exists to look at.
lenses: checks whose output does not depend on what they check
survivors.why: `npm run proposals` prints "The personal-data scan found nothing" and tells the operator "Read the labels before this file goes anywhere public" (scripts/proposals.ts:235-242). This repository is public, and CLAUDE.md §14 names precisely this channel: "Identification reads plates, and a label can come back carrying an address or a licence number." `modelRead` IS the plate reading — pass 3's own transcription of the label — and it is the half of the fixture the scan is blind to. A reviewer following the printed instruction reads the labels and never learns there is a second text column. `models[]` is documented at line 64 as the deprecated one ("no longer what rule 6 reads"); the scan reads the deprecated field and skips the current one.
survivors.evidence:
`scanForPersonalData` builds its field list from exactly two sources:

```ts
// proposalFixture.ts:231-234
const fields: { where: PersonalDataHit['where']; text: string }[] = [
  { where: 'label', text: p.label },
  ...p.models.map((m) => ({ where: 'model' as const, text: m })),
]
```

But `buildFixture` writes a third text field into every fixture (proposalFixture.ts:115):

```ts
...(p.modelRead ? { modelRead: p.modelRead } : {}),
```

and `PersonalDataHit.where` is typed `'label' | 'model'` (line 189), so there is structurally no value a hit could carry to name it.

Planted the thing the scan forbids and it did not fire:

```
$ node --import tsx test/_scratch_t1.ts
fixture proposal: {"id":"o1",...,"models":[],"modelRead":"Gas fitter licence 12345 613-555-0142 at 1 Nowhere Road"}
scan hits: []
```

That string contains all three of the shapes the scan claims to catch (licence-by-word, phone, address) and produced zero hits, because it is in the unread field.

The committed public fixture already carries the field, and carries it more often than the one that IS scanned:

```
$ node -e "...fixtures/proposals/mechanical-room_pass3-rerun_2026-08-13.json..."
proposals: 50  carrying modelRead: 15
sample modelRead values: [ '45MHP1B1STAA', 'WOB5 PC1', '600545B', 'G9-60SDE-30 260', 'DMF150', 'UT-450 CE', ... ]
carrying models[]: 7
```

The test that claims whole-run coverage cannot see it either — `proposal-fixture.test.ts:190` ("is clean on the whole of a real run") builds its proposals through `fromDb`, which hardcodes `models: []` (line 80) and never sets `modelRead`, so that assertion exercises label text only.
corrections:
Two magnitude details in the claim need tightening; neither touches the verdict.

(a) "re-running the scan over the committed fixture now examines 15 additional strings that were previously unexamined" — 15 additional strings would be examined, but 8 of the 15 `modelRead` values appear verbatim inside their own `label` and were therefore already covered incidentally. The genuinely unexamined surface in that committed fixture is 7 strings (e.g. `WOB5 PC1`, `UT-450 CE`, `EWPS20B20`, `UP826-990`, `TSMS-4/8`, `1601706`), not 15. Adding the field produces no new hits on that fixture (verified: 0), so the fix costs nothing in false positives.

(b) "the scan reads the deprecated field and skips the current one" — accurate about scoring (line 63-65: `models[]` is "no longer what rule 6 reads"), but `models[]` is not dead data: `server/scripts/proposals.ts:105` repopulates it from pass-1 plate claims on every write and both committed fixtures carry it. So the scan is not idle; it reads a live but structurally-filtered field and misses the unfiltered free-text one.

The finding stands as stated. One wording correction: the claim calls models[] "the deprecated one". Line 64's comment says models[] is "Kept, and no longer what rule 6 reads" — that is superseded FOR SCORING, not deprecated as data; proposals.ts:104-105 still populates it live from plate claims on every write. The accurate framing is that the scan covers pass 1's photograph-level model strings and is blind to pass 3's per-object model reading, not that it reads a dead field. That sharpens rather than weakens the finding: both are the same category of value (a model's transcription of a plate), which is exactly why the scan already has a `where: 'model'` case, and why omitting the second is an oversight rather than a scope decision.

survivors.title: `read.ts` and `match.ts` report stored state through a `report()` that takes no run outcome, so it cannot distinguish "this run found these" from "this run did nothing" — the exact bug fixed in their sibling `resolve.ts` and nowhere else.
lenses: checks whose output does not depend on what they check
survivors.why: Pass 1 and pass 3 are the two passes that cost money and send photographs of the inside of a house. A run whose calls all fail (401, spend cap, transport) still ends with `Ran 0, failed 16` followed by a confident table of labels or objects from an earlier run — the same presentation that already misled a runner session on 2026-08-13 in pass 2. `read.ts`'s and `match.ts`'s plan-only paths are worse than pass 2's: they print the table after a command that by definition ran nothing, with no qualifier at all. Verification-discipline rule 5 and rule 13 both say the fix for this class is applied to the class; here it was applied to the one file the incident happened in.
corrections:
Two corrections to the evidence as stated; neither weakens the finding.

1. The claim says "read.ts's only comment on `report` is about function hoisting at line 82-84." That is wrong. read.ts:213-219 carries a docstring on `report`, and its first line is "What pass 1 found, read back from the tables rather than from the answer." match.ts:179 also has one: "/** The two lanes, printed apart — because that is the whole point of the pass. */". Neither is a defence of the omission: read.ts's "Deliberately" defends a different choice (not grouping labels into objects, which would be pass 3's job), and match.ts's defends the two-lane layout. read.ts's first line makes the finding stronger rather than weaker — the author recorded in a comment that the table is stored state and did not put that fact where the runner reads it, which is the signature failure class exactly (a value being known is not a reader being able to reach it).

2. "changes their output on exactly two inputs — the plan-only path and a drain where result.ran === 0" understates it by one. resolve.ts's fixed report has three branches: ran === 0 (resolve.ts:174), ran > 0 && failed > 0 (resolve.ts:180, "⚠ N job(s) failed this run. The table below is complete storage, so it includes work those jobs did not do."), and the silent case. A class sweep of read.ts and match.ts changes output on three input classes, not two.

3. Scope note, offered rather than claimed: the same shape appears at passes.ts:186-192, where the end-of-run summary "N labels read · N products resolved · N plate-derived" is read from `readings`, `product_resolutions` and `objects` by import_id with no run-outcome qualifier — though passes.ts does print per-pass `ran/failed` and a failure line at passes.ts:150-152, which is more mitigation than read.ts or match.ts carry. score.ts is not affected: its report(proposals, header) is a function of its argument.

Scope refinement only, the claim itself stands: server/scripts/identify.ts has the same shape on its run path — :334-336 prints `result.ran`/`result.failed`, then :369 prints `${objects.length} objects proposed` read straight from the objects table with no `ran === 0` qualifier. So "the fix landed in resolve.ts and nowhere else" is exact, but the unswept class is three scripts, not two (identify.ts's exposure is run-path only; read.ts and match.ts are exposed on both the run path and the plan-only path). Also worth stating precisely: on the --run path read.ts and match.ts do print `Ran X, failed Y` immediately above the table — the finding is not that the outcome is invisible, it is that the table is not attached to it, which is exactly the configuration that misled the runner in resolve.ts before 66325cc.

survivors.title: `SCANNED_ROOTS` excludes `server/scripts`, so doctrine scans that claim "anywhere in the codebase" and "at all" cannot see 2,700 lines of database-touching code — and three files there break one of them.
lenses: checks whose output does not depend on what they check
survivors.why: These scans are this repo's stated mechanism for doctrine that no behavioural test can reach — "the way this doctrine breaks is not by someone deciding to render proposals, it is by a read path quietly joining ai_generations for convenience." Two of the three reads have arguments beside them (match.ts:138-148 argues for printing unmodelled keys; smoke.ts reads the cost ledger), but none of them is an exemption anybody made: they are outside the scan's reach, so the green result is not evidence for the sentence the test's name asserts. The `NOT_SCANNED` map at line 57 shows the repo's own convention — an exclusion is a declared decision with a reason — and no such declaration exists for this root.
survivors.evidence:
```ts
// doctrine.test.ts:136-140
/** The roots any scan walks. Kept here so the audit below can walk them all. */
const SCANNED_ROOTS = [
  join(repoRoot, 'server', 'src'),
  join(repoRoot, 'web', 'src'),
]
```

The comment is not true: one scan does walk `server/scripts` (line 3015, the `HOUSESTEADY_OPERATOR` check), which is why the directory is known to be scannable. Every other scan is scoped to `serverSrc`, including ones whose titles claim repo-wide reach — line 160 `'never UPDATEs or DELETEs a captured row, anywhere in the codebase'`, and:

```ts
// doctrine.test.ts:586-596
it('lets only the acceptance path read ai_generations at all', () => {
  const ALLOWED = [join('ai','accept.ts'), join('ai','queue.ts'), join('overlay','store.ts')]
  const offenders = sourceFiles(serverSrc)
    .filter((f) => /\bai_generations\b/.test(codeOf(f)))
    .filter((f) => !ALLOWED.some((a) => f.endsWith(a)))
  assert.deepEqual(offenders, [], 'a read path touching ai_generations is how an unsigned value reaches the screen')
})
```

Re-running that exact predicate with `server/scripts` added to the walk:

```
offenders if the walk included server/scripts:
  server/scripts/match.ts       // SELECT output FROM ai_generations ... and prints the raw output
  server/scripts/proposals.ts   // SELECT id, task, created_at FROM ai_generations
  server/scripts/smoke.ts       // SELECT model, input_tokens, ... FROM ai_generations
```

I applied the other two source-shape scans to the same extended walk to size the gap honestly — the actor-column scan and the inline-prompt scan both come back empty, and `make-fixture.ts`'s `'claude-sonnet-5'` literals are fixture data rather than a model call. So the concrete count today is three, all against the one scan that says "at all". `SCANNED_ROOTS` also feeds the extension audit at line 2825, so `server/scripts` is outside that too: a `.tsx` or a new extension appearing there would not be declared or refused.
corrections:
Two corrections, neither fatal.

1. The FALSIFIABLE AS clause says "the actor-column and model-id scans stay green." The actor-column scan does. The **model-ID scan does not**: doctrine.test.ts:566-574 is a bare regex over comment-stripped code, and server/scripts/make-fixture.ts:552, :677 and :679 carry `model: 'claude-sonnet-5'` and `actorId: 'claude-sonnet-5'` as live object literals, not comments. So adding `server/scripts` to `SCANNED_ROOTS` produces a **fourth** decision to make, not three — an exemption for a fixture generator whose literals are simulated field-app chat records rather than a model call. The finding's prose sized this honestly ("fixture data rather than a model call"); only its prediction line contradicts itself.

2. "The comment is not true" is right but worth stating precisely: `SCANNED_ROOTS`'s first sentence ("The roots any scan walks") is false — doctrine.test.ts:3015 walks a root not in the list, and object-lanes.test.ts:164-166 walks its own pair — while its second sentence ("Kept here so the audit below can walk them all") describes its only actual consumer, the extension audit at :2827. The defect is the overclaiming first sentence plus the untrue test name at :586, not the constant's existence.

Two corrections of degree, neither touching the core.

(a) The falsifiability statement is wrong on one half. It predicts "the actor-column and model-id scans stay green." The actor-column scan does stay green (I applied the CAPTURED_TABLES UPDATE/DELETE predicate to server/scripts: zero hits). The model-id scan at `doctrine.test.ts:566-574` does NOT — extending it to server/scripts turns it red naming `server/scripts/make-fixture.ts`, whose lines 552, 677 and 679 carry `'claude-sonnet-5'` literals. The finder noted this in prose and then contradicted it in the prediction. The honest prediction is: adding server/scripts turns TWO scans red — one on a genuine undeclared gap (three files, `ai_generations`) and one on synthetic manifest fixture data that would need either an exemption entry or a scan that distinguishes a fixture's `model` field from a model call.

(b) "Three files break one of them" is right as against the rule the test's name states, but the three are not equally severe and the finding should not be read as three unsigned values reaching a client. Only `match.ts:152` reads the generation's `output`, and it prints unmodelled keys to an operator terminal under an argued comment. `proposals.ts:159` reads id/task/created_at metadata only. `smoke.ts:167` reads the cost ledger — which `visitSpend` at `server/src/ai/queue.ts:259` already exposes from inside ALLOWED, so that one is a reinvented read with a sanctioned home. Nothing here is client-facing. The defect is that all three sit outside the scan's reach, so none of them is an exemption anybody made.

One addition worth carrying: `SCANNED_ROOTS` has exactly one consumer, the extension audit at line 2827, so the concrete blast radius today is that a new extension under `server/scripts` — a `.tsx`, a `.mjs`, a `.json` — would be neither walked by the operator scan at 3015 (which only returns `.ts`/`.tsx`) nor flagged as unaccounted by the audit, and no `NOT_SCANNED` entry would record the decision.

survivors.title: Sixteen slots the binder draft can never fill are rendered as "The producer exists and the visit did not supply it", which blames the visit for missing software.
lenses: Client-facing overclaim — every rendered sentence held against the provenance behind it, across `server/src/report/**`, `server/scripts/binder.ts`, and the House Style lint that gates them.
survivors.why: This document exists to be critiqued by an outside reviewer, and binderDraft.ts:29-34 states the whole reason the reasons are carried: "*Nothing here because no lab result has returned* is a different fact from *nothing here because nobody has built the producer*, and **an outside reviewer can only critique the second**." Sixteen of the twenty-seven gaps are sorted into the half the reviewer cannot act on, and binder.ts:183-186 then prints "⚑ 8 of the 27 gaps are missing PRODUCERS rather than missing data — ... they are what an outside review is for", steering attention away from them by name. The document also carries a claim about the software that is false, in a file whose own comment (binder.ts:118) calls this "a heading in a client-facing draft".
survivors.evidence:
server/src/report/binderDraft.ts:172-182 —
  emptyReason = data.noProducer.has(slot.id)
    ? 'no-producer'
    : data.awaiting?.has(slot.id)
      ? 'no-data-yet'
      : 'not-captured'
  ...
      : '**GAP — this ought to be here and is not.** The producer exists and the visit did not supply it.'

The caller supplies `noProducer` from a hand-kept list and never supplies `awaiting` at all — server/scripts/binder.ts:137-140:
  const draft = buildDraft(schema, profile, {
    counts,
    noProducer: new Set(Object.keys(NO_PRODUCER)),
  })

And `counts` (binder.ts:105-126) has exactly four keys: s7.components, s4.profile, s12.alarms, s10.findings. Every other slot is structurally zero no matter what the visit contained, so `not-captured` is the default branch for everything the hand-kept list forgot.

Run on both committed fixtures, 19 of the 27 gaps take that branch; 16 of them have no count entry at all:
  s1.shutoff-map · s1.response-procedures · s1.emergency-contacts · s2.property-summary ·
  s2.top-items · s2.tests-in-flight · s2.services-due · s2.missing-records · s2.next-review ·
  s6.profile · s11.warranties · s12.egress · s12.other · s15.custom-schedule ·
  s15.owner-pro-split · s15.both-realities

No producer exists for them. `for s in s1.shutoff-map s1.emergency-contacts s2.top-items s6.profile s11.warranties s12.egress; do grep -rl "$s" --include=*.ts server/src server/scripts; done` returns nothing for any of them. (`s2.next-review` matches only server/src/report/renderGate.ts, which is a gate that refuses it, not a producer.)

binder.ts:76-86 checks the list in one direction only — every id in NO_PRODUCER must be a real slot id. Nothing checks the converse, which is the direction that produces this sentence.
corrections:
Two corrections, neither of which saves the code.

1. The proof method is wrong and the number 16 is too high. "grep for the slot id finds no producer" does not hold here: audit/run.ts is a generic schema-driven engine that names no slot ids, so it produces state for every slot without ever mentioning one. Three of the sixteen — s1.shutoff-map (sources ["field.pin.layer:shutoffs"]), s12.egress (["field.check:egress"]) and s12.other (["field"]) — are genuinely field-wired by the repo's own isWired, and "the producer exists and the visit did not supply it" is CORRECT for them. The right instrument is sources.ts::unwiredNote, not grep.

Applying it, the sixteen split three ways:
- Flatly false (unwiredNote returns UNWIRED; the input is not a visit output at all): s6.profile, s11.warranties, s1.response-procedures, s2.next-review. Plus s15.both-realities, which run.ts:456 separately calls underivable.
- False transitively (nominally "wired" only because sources.ts:isSlotReference short-circuits on /^s\d+/, while the referenced slot is itself in NO_PRODUCER): s1.emergency-contacts → s17.directory, s2.top-items → s10.concerns, s2.tests-in-flight → s13.tests, s2.services-due → s15.default-schedule, s2.missing-records → s5.index.
- Correct as rendered: s1.shutoff-map, s12.egress, s12.other. (s2.property-summary, s15.custom-schedule and s15.owner-pro-split are arguable — their inputs partly exist and nothing derives them, so they are missing-producer rather than missing-visit-data, but the case is weaker.)

So roughly ten to thirteen of the sixteen carry a false sentence, not sixteen. The header claim should read "at least ten", and the two named exemplars should be s6.profile and s11.warranties (intake form and client documents — §3 inputs a visit can never supply), not s1.shutoff-map.

2. The mechanism, restated precisely. The defect is not that NO_PRODUCER is short — §15 is a doctrine-vs-code table and was never an enumeration of unbuilt producers, so it is being used to decide a question it does not answer. The defect is that binderDraft.ts derives the reason from set membership when the schema already carries the answer, and the repo already has the module that reads it. The fix is one import: replace `noProducer: new Set(Object.keys(NO_PRODUCER))` with a set computed from unwiredNote over the schema's slots, union the transitively-dead slot references, and keep NO_PRODUCER only for slots whose sources look wired but whose producer is genuinely unbuilt. That also makes the one-directional guard at binder.ts:78-86 unnecessary rather than incomplete.

Secondary limb worth keeping: `awaiting` is never passed by any caller, so `no-data-yet` (binderDraft.ts:180-181) is unreachable outside the unit test — a documented three-state design of which production can express two.

Three adjustments, one of which makes the finding worse.

(a) The count of gaps no visit can ever change is SEVENTEEN, not sixteen. binder.ts:125 is `['s10.findings', one('SELECT COUNT(*) AS n FROM audit_slots WHERE 1 = 0')]` — a count key hardwired to zero, with no comment defending it. So s10.findings also prints "The producer exists and the visit did not supply it" forever; it merely has a key, unlike the other sixteen.

(b) Minor accuracy note on the evidence as written: the claim's grep sentence holds for the six ids it names, but four of the sixteen DO appear under server/src — in comments only, never as producers: server/src/audit/run.ts:243-244 (s2.services-due, s15.owner-pro-split, s15.custom-schedule) and server/src/audit/schema.ts:74 (s1.response-procedures). This does not change the finding.

(c) Framing precision: for a few of the sixteen the field manifest IS a readable source (sources.ts's `field` reader has a count), so `unwiredNote` calls s1.shutoff-map, s12.egress and s12.other "wired" and the audit engine does bind pins to them. The accurate statement is therefore not "no producer exists anywhere in the repo for all sixteen" but "the binder draft has no reader for any of the sixteen, so no visit to any house can change that sentence" — and for at least four of them the repo's own oracle in sources.ts says the input is not readable at all.

survivors.title: The House Style lint's condition-grade rule only matches the colon form, so "in poor condition" reaches a signed client document.
lenses: Client-facing overclaim — every rendered sentence held against the provenance behind it, across `server/src/report/**`, `server/scripts/binder.ts`, and the House Style lint that gates them.
survivors.why: "No condition grading" is doctrine, not preference — CLAUDE.md §7 and the Object/Concern Model §7 both name it as a judgement the concierge cannot defend and the homeowner may act on. The lint runs in the render path precisely so it sees "the sentence a concierge types into the editor at four o'clock on a Friday" (houseStyle.ts:8-9), and that sentence is written in English, not in enum syntax. The rule catches the machine spelling of the grade and misses the human one, so the only form that can actually occur is the form that ships.
survivors.evidence:
server/src/report/houseStyle.ts:109-116 —
  {
    name: 'a condition grade',
    pattern: /\bcondition\s*[::]\s*(poor|fair|good|excellent)\b/i,
    because:
      'House Style §7 and the Object/Concern Model §7 — a grade is a judgement a concierge ' +
      'cannot defend and a homeowner may act on. ...'
  },

Run against `lint(text, 'a typed row in "Missing from you"')` (probe via npx tsx, since deleted):
  PASSES "The rear deck is in poor condition."
  PASSES "The roof is in fair condition and the soffit is in good condition."
  CAUGHT "Condition: poor"

Same run, other constructions House Style names by name:
  PASSES "This needs immediate attention."   (§8: "Alarming is adjectives and urgency: serious, dangerous, immediately, before something happens" — the severity pattern at houseStyle.ts:76 has serious and dangerous, not immediately)
  PASSES "The panel is a fire hazard."       (pattern has `hazardous`, not `hazard`)
  PASSES "The water heater should be replaced."

The rendering path is live: render.ts:201 lints every typed row — `for (const text of column.typed) violations.push(...lint(text, ...))` — and typed rows are what the whole "Missing from you" column ships as (draft.ts:14-20). The test that covers this rule pins the same single form: server/test/render.test.ts:226 — `['Condition: poor', 'a condition grade']`.
corrections:
Two adjustments to how the finding should be stated, neither of which weakens it:

(a) Scope it precisely. The rule does not miss "the English form" generically — it misses every construction where the grade is not colon-bound to the word: adjective-before ("in poor condition"), copular ("the deck condition is poor"), and colon-with-intervening-words ("Condition of the deck: poor"). It does catch a leading or mid-sentence colon form and a full-width colon, and its value list already runs beyond House Style's own row (`excellent` is code-added). So the accurate statement is: the author generalised the grade vocabulary and left the syntax pinned to one shape.

(b) Drop "The water heater should be replaced." from the evidence. Neither House Style §11's checkable list nor §7's table bans a recommendation from a human writer — §4/§11 bar *AI* from proposing recommendation, which is a different gate. Carrying it weakens the finding. "This needs immediate attention." is a genuine sibling gap (§8 line 116 names *immediately* by name as alarming and houseStyle.ts:76 has no immediate/immediately), but it belongs to the severity rule, not this one, and should be reported as its own instance of the same shape rather than folded in here.

The core finding stands as stated; two supporting bullets overstate and should be trimmed. "Other constructions House Style names by name" holds only for `immediately` (prompts/house-style/v001.md:107, §8 alarming). `hazard`/`hazardous` is not in House Style at all — §7's list is "code violation, non-compliant, unsafe", and `hazardous` at houseStyle.ts:76 is the lint's own addition, so "The panel is a fire hazard." passing is a near-miss inside the lint rather than a rule House Style names. "The water heater should be replaced." is likewise not named by House Style §7 or §8. Also, "the only form that can actually occur is the form that ships" is slightly too strong — the colon form can occur in pasted or tabulated text; the accurate statement is that the prose form is the one a person types and it is the one that passes. Scope is wider than the claim says: the same hole is in renderGate.ts:204 and :255, so a binder slot's `renderNote` carrying "in poor condition" is equally renderable. Falsifiable fix check: adding a prose alternation (e.g. `/\bin (poor|fair|good|excellent) condition\b/i` alongside the existing pattern) should make the probe throw HouseStyleRefused with rule 'a condition grade' and leave `editions(db, propertyId).length === 0`, while still passing render.test.ts:226.

survivors.title: The property label reaches the client document's title unlinted, because the lint reads `address ?? label` and the title always reads `label`.
lenses: Client-facing overclaim — every rendered sentence held against the provenance behind it, across `server/src/report/**`, `server/scripts/binder.ts`, and the House Style lint that gates them.
survivors.why: The `<title>` is client-facing: it is the browser tab on the link the editor hands over (GapReport.tsx:130, `api.editionUrl(e.id)`) and it is what most browsers print into the header when the page is saved as PDF. The lint was extended to the footer precisely because "the first render put `op-dp` in the footer" (render.ts:127-131) — the same class, one field over, and this one is an operator-typed free-text field, which is exactly where a banned word gets in.
survivors.evidence: The lint (render.ts:205-206): violations.push(...lint(args.signedByName, 'the signature line')) violations.push(...lint(args.property.address ?? args.property.label, 'the address in the header')) The render (render.ts:337 and 369): Gap report — ${esc(args.property.label)} ...Gap report${esc(args.property.address ?? args.property.label)}... So whenever `address` is non-null — the normal case, and what the repo's own test fixtures use — `label` is composed into the document and never linted. Confirmed by signing an edition with `property: { label: 'The Smith place — recurring damp issue', address: '14 Dundas Street West' }` (probe via npx tsx, since deleted): SIGNED, no House Style refusal. TITLE: Gap report — The Smith place — recurring damp issue "issue" is rule one of the lint (houseStyle.ts:68-73) and House Style §7 bans it outright.
corrections: The finding stands as stated; two sharpenings. (1) The hole is precisely the address-set case — when address is null, `address ?? label` does lint the label, so the check passes exactly when the field is absent and lapses when it is present. (2) The evidence text says "five call sites (lines 197, 198, 199, 201, 205, 206)" — that is six lines; the count is wrong, the lines are right, and none reads property.label unconditionally. Worth adding to the finding: the doctrine scan at doctrine.test.ts:1372-1385 names render.test.ts as the compensating check for render.ts's by-name exemption, and that check reads only `html.slice(html.indexOf('<body>'))` — so the <title> is uncovered by the source scan, by its own stated substitute, and by the lint. Three checks, one blind spot, which is the signature shape: the lint value is computed, and the reader's path to the title never passes through it.

Two points of precision, neither of which changes the verdict. (a) The label is not universally unlinted — it is unlinted exactly when `address` is non-null. With `address === null` the `??` fallback at render.ts:206 sends the label through the lint, so the label-only property is protected and the fully-filled-in property is not. That inversion is worth stating in the finding, because the repo's own UI hint (web/src/pages/Properties.tsx:49-53) actively urges operators to fill the address in: "The address is worth filling in… the address is what the builder compares against to catch a visit filed under the wrong house." Following the app's advice is what removes the label from the lint's reach. (b) The evidence's parenthetical says "five call sites (lines 197, 198, 199, 201, 205, 206)" — that is six lines, and there are two more in renderGate.ts. The count is wrong; the conclusion drawn from it is not — I re-ran the grep repo-wide and none of the eight reads `property.label` unconditionally. Scope note for whoever fixes it: `

${esc(column.title)}

` at render.ts:315 is also interpolated unlinted, but column titles come from declared draft config rather than an operator's keyboard, so it is a different and much weaker class. `property.label` is the one free-text field that reaches the document without passing the gate.

survivors.title: The in-code default group frame still carries the exact wording the design session retracted as a not-accessible claim over not-inspected data.

survivors.evidence:
server/src/report/names.ts:60-66 —

    default: one(block.default) ?? {
      withRoom: 'In {room}, we were not able to cover:',
      withoutRoom: 'We were not able to cover:',

The code fallback is reached whenever the shipped file has no `frames` block or its `default` fails the shape check at names.ts:48-51 (`typeof f.withRoom === 'string' && typeof f.withoutRoom === 'string'`) — a renamed key or a typo is enough, and `framesOf` neither warns nor refuses. Malformed `byReason` entries are dropped the same silent way (names.ts:55-58).

The test written to prevent exactly this claim runs only against the shipped file: server/test/render.test.ts:66-73 loads `loadClientNames()` with its default path, so it exercises the JSON and never the fallback. The finding stands, but its FALSIFIABLE-AS scenario is wrong and must not be repeated as written.

CLAIMED: "deleting or renaming the `frames` key ... with no warning, no lint violation, and render.test.ts's not-reached guard still green because it reads the shipped file."

I ran it. I copied schema/client-names-v1.json aside, deleted the `frames` key, and ran `npx tsx --test server/test/render.test.ts`: 4 of 16 fail, including `not ok 2 - never lets a not-reached frame claim we tried and were blocked` — the guard the claim says stays green. Because that guard reads the shipped file, mutating the shipped file is exactly what it sees; with `frames` gone, `byReason` is empty, every group takes the code fallback, and the guard's `/not able|could not|unable/i` fires. doctrine.test.ts:1896 also throws on `file.frames.default`. So the whole-block case IS caught by the suite.

THE ACTUAL UNGUARDED PATH IS NARROWER AND I DEMONSTRATED IT. Two conditions, both live:
(1) a shape error confined to `frames.default` — one misspelled key. I renamed `withRoom` to `with_room` and left `byReason` intact: `npx tsx --test server/test/render.test.ts server/test/doctrine.test.ts` → 133 pass, 0 fail. doctrine.test.ts:1896 only asserts `file.frames.default` is truthy, never its shape; render.test.ts's not-reached and no-access assertions read `byReason`, which is untouched. Nothing anywhere sees it.
(2) a group whose reason is not one of the three declared in `byReason` — which the repo's own fail-open vocabulary doctrine guarantees is possible: carriedItems.ts:65-69 carries "the na reason id verbatim... a config that declares a gap-feeding reason this builder has never met produces a row carrying that reason's own id".

With (1) in place I passed a row with `reason: 'weather-window'` through `clientGroups` using the real `loadClientNames()` and `naLabelMap()`:
  FRAME  : "In ensuite, we were not able to cover:"
  LABEL  : not-inspected
  NEXT   : undefined
  LINT   : []
The label is correct and the sentence the homeowner reads is not — both retracted claims at once (the obstruction claim and the missing article), no closer, no lint violation, no warning, and a green suite.

Working tree restored: schema/client-names-v1.json md5 matches the original and `git status --porcelain` is empty.

Two amendments, neither of which rescues the code. (a) The stated falsification is inaccurate in one particular: deleting or renaming the whole `frames` key is NOT unwarned. server/test/doctrine.test.ts:1893 does `file.frames.default` against the shipped file and throws `Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'default')`, turning the suite red — I ran that assertion against the mutated object and confirmed it throws. The genuinely silent path is one level down: renaming or typoing a key INSIDE `frames.default` (e.g. `withRoom` -> `with_room`) leaves `file.frames.default` truthy and `byReason` non-empty, so doctrine.test.ts:1885-1897 stays green while `one(block.default)` at names.ts:48-51 returns null and the code fallback fires. In that state the retracted wording reaches only groups whose `reason` is absent from `byReason` — today `not-reached`, `no-access` and `deferred` are all declared, so it takes a config-declared na reason id that the frames file does not map, which carriedItems.ts:186-198 makes an ordinary expected case. So the failure is narrower than claimed and still silent, still unlinted, still invisible to every test. (b) The finding understates the miss: the code copy also failed the second ratified correction. schema/client-names-v1.json:54 `articleNote` records `In ensuite, we were not able to cover` as 'what the first render produced and it reads wrong' and the shipped frames all carry 'In the {room}'; names.ts:62 reads `'In {room}, we were not able to cover:'` with no article. The code fallback carries both retracted forms, which is the class-of-wording sweep landing on one copy and not the other.

It is also doctrine 6: three ids the caller supplied were dropped with no warning.

server/src/report/binderDraft.ts:161-176 —

It is a deliberate, tested, commented decision (`server/test/binder-draft.test.ts:98-99`), the caller agrees with it (`server/scripts/binder.ts:52`), and its rendered sentence launders nothing. survivors.title: Desk-work timing is fully built — table, module, three routes, tests — and nothing anywhere can start or stop a span.
lenses: Free sweep — first-tour reading of server/src, server/scripts, schema/, prompts/ and web/src, plus a real end-to-end run of the pipeline (import the walk fixture → audit → gap-report draft → signed edition → binder draft) to compare what the code computes against what a reader actually receives.

survivors.evidence:
server/src/desk/work.ts:14 claims the outcome: "Ten houses in, the pricing basis exists without anyone having sat and measured it, and it keeps calibrating as concierges get faster."

The writers are `startWork` (work.ts:116) and `stopWork` (work.ts:154), exposed at server/src/index.ts:1020 (`POST /api/properties/:id/desk-work/start`) and index.ts:1042 (`POST /api/desk-work/:spanId/stop`), reading at index.ts:1006.

The routes exist so that surface can call them when it is built. survivors.title: `EditionColumn.media` is computed and stored on every signed edition and rendered by nothing — and it is built from the one field draft.ts marks "never reaches a client".
lenses: Free sweep — first-tour reading of server/src, server/scripts, schema/, prompts/ and web/src, plus a real end-to-end run of the pipeline (import the walk fixture → audit → gap-report draft → signed edition → binder draft) to compare what the code computes against what a reader actually receives.

Computed on every signed edition, render.ts:184: media: mediaLines(rows), declared at render.ts:89 as "/** What the room holds, once per room rather than once per row. */", and stored into `report_editions.composition`. The HTML composer ignores it entirely — render.ts:317-333: const body = args.columns .filter((c) => c.groups.length > 0 || c.typed.length > 0) .map((column) => { ... return `

${esc(column.title)}

${groups}${typed}

It is also unreachable from the desk: GapReport.tsx reads `row.media` (the draft row, lines 334-345) and `e.withheld.length` (line 135), never `columns[].media`. No test in server/test references it. And the location it composes is the wrong register — render.ts:250-259: if (!byWhere.has(row.source.where)) byWhere.set(row.source.where, row) return [...byWhere].map(([where, row]) => ({ where, summary: ... })) against server/src/report/draft.ts:67-70: /** Desk display. May name a zone type; never reaches a client. */ where: string /** Client-safe, or null. What the render composes a location from. */ whereLabel: string | null
corrections:
The finding is real but should be narrowed to one prong. The second prong is overstated and I would cut it.

ACCURATE VERSION: `EditionColumn.media` (render.ts:90) is computed on every signed edition (render.ts:184 `media: mediaLines(rows)`), persisted into the immutable `report_editions.composition` blob, replayed by `editions()` and served over the API into a typed web field (web/src/api.ts:922) — and read by nothing in server/src, server/test, or web/src. `document()` receives it and ignores it. Migration 014:47-50 scopes composition to "Every group and item that went in… this is what it was made of"; media is neither, and the bytes never had it. That is the signature class exactly: computed value, no reader path, tests green because they check `.groups` and `.typed`.

WHAT I WOULD DROP: the "wrong register / loaded gun" argument. `mediaLines` grouping on `row.source.where` (render.ts:254) is not the whereLabel split failing to be carried — `where` is the CORRECT field for something that never reaches a client, and choosing it is evidence the author treated this as desk-side, not evidence of carelessness. The two halves of the claim are in tension: you cannot cite the desk-register field as proof of a client-leak risk while also proving the thing never renders. And the leak is hypothetical — it requires a future edit that renders the line. Note also the claim's implied premise that House Style would not catch it is true (prompts/house-style/v001.md contains no zone-type ban; the protection at gap-report.test.ts:322-323 comes from clientVoice.ts:147 using `whereLabel`, not from the lint) — but a hypothesis about a future edit is not a present defect and this repo's own rules exclude it.

ONE FACTUAL CORRECTION to the evidence given: "No test in server/test references it" is loosely stated. Tests do read `edition.columns` — render.ts's own suite at render.test.ts:45, 69, 94, 109, 140, 161 — but exclusively `.groups` and `.typed`. The claim's conclusion is unaffected; its supporting grep was just too narrow.

The finding stands; three precisions.
