survivors.title: Every edition records `house_style_version` as a hardcoded string literal that no code derives, hashes, or checks — including in the test that would catch drift.
lenses: Free sweep — first-tour reading of server/src, server/scripts, schema/, prompts/ and web/src, plus a real end-to-end run of the pipeline (import the walk fixture → audit → gap-report draft → signed edition → binder draft) to compare what the code computes against what a reader actually receives.
survivors.why: prompts/README.md states the rule this is meant to satisfy: "Every artifact records which prompt version produced it" and "Changing a prompt means changing its version." Today an edition's claim about which writing standard produced it is a sentence typed once, not a fact derived from anything. Cut `prompts/house-style/v002.md`, or edit a rule inside `server/src/report/houseStyle.ts` (which is where the lint actually lives), and every subsequent edition still says `house-style/v001` — so "why does this binder read differently from that one", the question §9 says must always be answerable, is answered wrongly and confidently. This is Verification Discipline rule 9 in the repo's own terms: a document asserting a checked state that carries the claim instead of the check, with two sides that cannot disagree.
survivors.evidence:
server/src/index.ts:918, inside the sign route:
      clientNames: { version: names.version, hash: names.hash },
      houseStyleVersion: 'house-style/v001',

Note the asymmetry on the two lines: client names carry a version AND a content hash read from the file; house style carries a literal and no hash. migration 014_editions.sql:43-46 introduces both under one comment — "What produced it, so a difference between two editions is explicable" — and declares `house_style_version TEXT NOT NULL` with no hash column beside it.

Nothing reads the file. index.ts imports no prompt loader at all (`grep -n prompts server/src/index.ts` -> no matches). `loadPrompts` (server/src/ai/prompts.ts:62) does load `prompts/house-style/v001.md` and compute its sha256 — that value exists in memory at runtime and is never asked for; `currentPrompt` is only ever called with the nine AI task names.

And the check cannot fail: server/test/render.test.ts:30 and :252 both pass the same literal `'house-style/v001'`.
corrections:
Accurate version: the sign route records the edition's writing standard as a hand-typed literal (server/src/index.ts:918) rather than reading it from the prompt library, and migration 014_editions.sql:43-46 gives it no hash column although the client-names value one line above carries both a version and a sha256 of the file as read (server/src/report/names.ts:76-80). The prompt library computes exactly this id, version and hash (server/src/ai/prompts.ts:62-102) but index.ts imports no prompt loader, so the value is computed at runtime in the worker and unreachable at the point it is recorded — the signature failure class.

The drift is NOT silent, and that part of the original claim is wrong: doctrine.test.ts:3075 pins `'house-style': 'v001'` and :3096 re-derives it from the directory, so adding prompts/house-style/v002.md fails the suite (verified: 116 pass, 1 fail). The residual defect is narrower and still real — that pin obliges a human to update LIVE, not index.ts:918. A deliberate go-live to v002 therefore ends with a green suite and every subsequent edition asserting `house-style/v001`. In-place edits to prompts/house-style/v001.md, and edits to the lint rules in server/src/report/houseStyle.ts (which carries no version at all), are caught by nothing.

A narrow residual survives, and it is not what was claimed. Adding a house-style version is caught. What is not caught is the *second* step of a deliberate go-live: if someone ships `prompts/house-style/v002.md` AND updates `LIVE` at server/test/doctrine.test.ts:3075 to `'v002'` — which is the acknowledged path the pin is designed to force — then server/src/index.ts:918 still writes `houseStyleVersion: 'house-style/v001'` and nothing ties the literal to the library. Accurate statement: "index.ts:918 hardcodes the house-style version rather than reading `currentPrompt(prompts, 'house-style').version`, so a deliberate, already-acknowledged version bump has one remaining place a person must remember to edit." That is a one-line hardening of an existing guard, not a claim that no guard exists — and it is a long way from "a sentence typed once, not a fact derived from anything," whose stated observable (suite stays green) is false.

survivors.evidence:
$ grep -rn "neverAI|aiMayDraft|specificityRule|recordFields|completeWhen" --include='*.ts' --include='*.tsx' server/src server/scripts web/src
(no output — zero hits for all five)

One slot, two declarations. The second is enforced by `renderGate.ts`'s branded `GatedValue` — I ran the gate against the shipped schema and both declaring slots clear, so that half demonstrably works. The first is enforced by nothing.

Also s10.concerns (schema lines 878-893):

  "neverAI": ["urgency", "planning-cost-range", "recommended-action"],

`specificityRule` even has an implementation — server/src/audit/completeness.ts:219, `watchScheduleShortfall(record, requires)`, headed "§10's specificity rule — a completeness rule, not style advice." corrections: The finding stands but should be re-pointed: the sharp end is s10.concerns and specificityRule, not the reserve figure. (a) s19.reserve-figure's `neverAI: true` is closest to a RESTATEMENT of an already-structural fact rather than a lone unenforced guard — the slot declares `sources: ["human"]` (schema:1116-1117), `sources` IS read (server/src/audit/sources.ts:125,141; run.ts:448), and the `ai` source prefix carries an explicit deliberate no-reader at sources.ts:71-79 routing every AI value through a human-signed overlay. Deleting `neverAI` there loses a label, not a wall. (b) The real defect is s10.concerns (schema:863-897), which declares NO `sources` array at all, so the sources-level protection does not reach it, and whose `aiMayDraft`/`neverAI` split is field-level — a distinction `sources` structurally cannot express. (c) The strongest single instance is `specificityRule`: it is not documentation — it carries `"isCompletenessRule": true`, it has a named implementation (completeness.ts:219, headed "§10's specificity rule — a completeness rule, not style advice"), and docs/HouseSteady_Binder-Builder_Increment-3_Build-Spec_2026-07-27.md:241 lists "a watch-schedule concern without a measurement, cadence, or escalation trigger fails" as a required acceptance BEHAVIOUR, in a list whose other members (narrative slots never gapping, a shutoff with only a close-up failing) are all wired. So a build spec asks for the behaviour, the function exists, nothing invokes it, and the only test duplicates the schema's values instead of reading them. That is "a rule written, documented, tested and never once invoked" — the audited class exactly. (d) The claim's "no comment anywhere argues the omission is deliberate" should be qualified: the Property-Flags Code-Reply §6 documents why the GATE does not read `neverAI` (a precise new key was substituted for a loose two-slot pointer), which is defensible on its own terms but is not a defence of `neverAI` having no reader at all.

One sub-observation inside the claim is real, sharper than the headline, and survives every objection above — but it is a different finding and should be re-filed as one rather than carried as support for "unread AI guard-rails."

server/src/audit/completeness.ts:219 exports `watchScheduleShortfall(record, requires)`, headed "§10's specificity rule — a completeness rule, not style advice." Its only importer in the entire repo is server/test/completeness.test.ts:16. That is precisely the shape renderGate.ts:19-24 names as the repo's own recorded failure — "That is Table I — `audit/provenance.ts`, five exported functions built, tested, and called by nothing, idle for weeks with no test able to notice" — and I confirmed audit/provenance.ts is STILL imported only by server/test/provenance.test.ts, so Table I is unfixed and now has a sibling.

The sharper half is the test itself. server/test/completeness.test.ts:181 declares `const REQUIRES = ['measurement', 'cadence', 'namedEscalationTrigger']` as a literal, rather than reading `specificityRule.requires` from schema/binder-schema-v1.json:887-895. The schema's list and the tested list therefore cannot disagree — if the design session amends the specificity rule to four requirements, every assertion still passes. That is Verification Discipline's "a check whose two sides cannot disagree has not been passing," and unlike `neverAI` it is a live duplication today, not a missing future guard.

Two factual corrections to the claim as written, independent of the above:
- `recordFields` and `completeWhen` are not AI guard-rails. `recordFields` is the record-set's field list; s10's `completeWhen` is prose — "every concern links to a task, a project, or a watch schedule — nothing floats" (schema:897) — with no machine-parseable form. Including them in a headline about AI guard-rails inflates a five-key list from a two-key argument.
- `neverAI: true` at schema:1118 and `neverAI: [...]` at schema:882 are the only two machine-addressable declarations; the classD comparison the claim leans on cuts the other way, since schema/profiles/baseline-v1.json:57 lists "s2.top-items ordering" and "client conversation and handover" — neither of which is a slot id — showing what a human-planning declaration looks like in this repo.

refutedTitles.title: The Master Spec's watch-schedule specificity rule is implemented and declared in the schema, and no code path ever invokes it or reads the declaration.
killedBy:
The mechanical half of the claim is true and I confirmed it empirically — but it is not a defect, because three separate code-level surfaces explicitly declare that the consumer does not exist yet.

WHAT I VERIFIED (the claim's facts hold):
- `grep -rn "watchScheduleShortfall|specificityRule|isCompletenessRule|namedEscalationTrigger"` across the whole repo returns exactly: schema/binder-schema-v1.json:887-895, server/src/audit/completeness.ts:219, and four lines in server/test/completeness.test.ts. No production hit.
- server/src/audit/run.ts:23-25 imports `assessItem, assessSlot, gapList, naReasonsOf, rollUp` from completeness.js — `watchScheduleShortfall` is not in the import list. run.ts is the only caller of `assessSlot` (lines 235, 267, 276).
- server/src/engine/completeness.ts (a different file) has zero hits for watch/specificity/cadence/escalation.
- Nothing reads `slot.specificityRule`; `Slot` (server/src/audit/schema.ts:64-91) only carries it via the `[key: string]: unknown` index signature.
- I RAN the finder's falsification test: patched the schema's `requires` to `["measurement"]`, ran `npm test` → `# tests 1224 / # pass 1224 / # fail 0`. Then restored the file (`git status` clean). So yes, the schema declaration is behaviourally inert.

WHY IT IS STILL NOT A DEFECT — the defence, which the finder did not quote:
1. server/src/audit/run.ts:470-473, the record-set evidence builder, states the gating in code:
       if (slot.id !== 's7.components') {
         // Every other record-set is keyed on something this builder does not hold
         // yet — lab results, concerns (Increment 5, gated on v4), programs.
         return { evidence: { expected: 0, withRecord: 0, shortfalls: [] } }
       }
   Concerns are named, dated to an increment, and gated on manifest v4. There are no concern records for the rule to check.
2. server/scripts/binder.ts:46 lists it in a CHECKED hand-kept map: `'s10.concerns': 'concerns as records — §15: nothing implements them; `openConcerns` is typed `never[]`'`, and binder.ts:77-80 fails loudly if any id there is not a real slot id. server/src/report/binderDraft.ts:179 renders it as "**GAP — nothing in the builder can fill this yet.**" — asserted by server/test/binder-draft.test.ts:86-87.
3. CLAUDE.md §15 carries the row, under the convention that a row leaves by being built, never by being qualified.

The signature failure class is "a value being computed is not the same as a reader being able to reach it" — its harm is a reader silently misled. Here nothing is computed at runtime at all, and no reader is misled in either direction: every surface that could show a concern says out loud that concerns do not exist. This is a helper written ahead of a consumer that three places declare unbuilt, not a stranded value.

Second reason the singling-out fails: `specificityRule` is not uniquely inert. Its sibling keys on the same slot — `recordFields`, `aiMayDraft`, `neverAI`, `completeWhen` — return ZERO hits across server/ and web/ (I grepped). /schema is "the Master Spec as machine-readable data" (CLAUDE.md §13); declarative-only is the normal state of an unbuilt section's slot, so an unconsumed key there is a spec entry, not a broken wire.

refutedTitles.title: `product_resolutions.honesty` is written on every row and read by nothing, so the `Inferred` label the migration says must travel with the row does not travel.
killedBy:
Refuted on three independent grounds, the first of which kills the claim's mechanism outright.

(1) THE LABEL IS NOT DROPPED AT THE JOIN. The finding rests on "objects has no honesty column, so the Inferred claim is recorded once and dropped at the first join." server/src/db/migrations/025_object_lanes.sql:33 is that join: `ALTER TABLE objects ADD COLUMN resolution_id TEXT REFERENCES product_resolutions(id);` and 025:18-20 states its purpose — "`resolution_id` IS WHAT MAKES `plate` CHECKABLE. A plate-derived object with no resolution behind it is a claim about provenance with nothing supporting it, so the lane and its evidence arrive together or not at all." It is populated on every plate-lane row: matchComplete.ts:556-559 inserts `... 'plate', args.resolutionOf.get(l.product) ?? null, ...`. So the Inferred label sits one declared foreign key from any plate object — which is precisely what "the value travels with the row" means.

(2) `objects` LACKS AN HONESTY COLUMN DELIBERATELY, AND COPYING ONE THERE WOULD BE THE DEFECT. An object's honesty is set by the human act, not inherited from the AI proposal: 018_object_confirmation.sql:105-108 enforces `CHECK ((act='confirmed' AND honesty_label='Observed') OR (act='adopted' AND honesty_label='Inferred'))`, described there as "THE CONSTRAINT THAT IS THE POINT", and confirm.ts:43-46/141-144 writes it via `ACT_LABEL`. matchComplete.ts:555 inserts objects with `confirmed_by NULL` — they are proposals until a person signs. Inheriting `Inferred` onto the object row would pre-decide the label the confirmation act exists to set.

(3) THE READER IS THE BINDER RENDERER, WHICH DOES NOT EXIST, AND THE REPO SAYS SO. The comment quoted as evidence (024:65-67) names "whoever renders it". CLAUDE.md §15 lists "Rendering the binder itself (§10) — Nothing. The gap report and the session plan render; the binder does not" and rules "None of these is a defect." Writing the value ahead of its renderer is the documented intent. Also, every value in the column is constant by construction — lookup.ts:195 `export const HONESTY_LABELS = ['Inferred'] as const` and the SQL literal at resolveProduct.ts:327 — so a reader today would recover no information the schema does not already guarantee; the column earns its keep the day a second label exists, which lookup.ts:190-194 says arrives only with `source_url` and search, in the same change.

Also: the finding's own falsifier ("no SELECT anywhere names it") is literally false — server/test/resolve-product.test.ts:193 runs `SELECT product, kind, honesty, resolved FROM product_resolutions` and asserts `honesty: 'Inferred'` at :197.

Checked and found nothing client-facing that fabricates a label: `grep -rn "Inferred" server/src server/scripts web/src` returns only the writer, the doctrine comments, confirm.ts's ACT_LABEL, and scripts/resolve.ts:213 — an operator-facing sentence about the whole build ("Every row is labelled `Inferred` and none says Documented"), not a per-row render, and structurally true given HONESTY_LABELS.

The grep is right (no production SELECT names `honesty`; only server/test/resolve-product.test.ts:193 reads it back), but the two claims that make it a defect are both false.

(1) "Recorded once and dropped at the first join" is wrong. server/src/db/migrations/025_object_lanes.sql:33 — `ALTER TABLE objects ADD COLUMN resolution_id TEXT REFERENCES product_resolutions(id)` — and server/src/ai/tasks/matchComplete.ts:557,570 populate it on every plate object: `insert.run(id, …, 'plate', args.resolutionOf.get(l.product) ?? null, l.modelRead ?? null, at)`. `resolutionOf` is built at matchComplete.ts:725-733 from `SELECT p.product, p.id FROM product_resolutions p WHERE p.import_id = ? AND p.resolved = 1`, and matchComplete.ts:477 refuses any located entry whose product is not in `known.products` (`if (!known.products.has(product)) { unknownProducts.push(product); continue }`), so the key always hits and the FK is genuinely populated. 025's comment states the purpose: "`resolution_id` IS WHAT MAKES `plate` CHECKABLE. A plate-derived object with no resolution behind it is a claim about provenance with nothing supporting it." The label travels by reference; nothing discards it.

(2) There is no reader today that gets a wrong or missing label, because no product-rendering surface exists at all. server/src/index.ts has no route touching `objects` or `product_resolutions` (routes: operators, properties, visits, imports, overlays, pass, memory, assists, media, report — grep "FROM objects" in index.ts returns nothing). web/src has no product surface. server/scripts/binder.ts:122-125 renders counts only (`SELECT COUNT(*) AS n FROM objects WHERE import_id = ? AND derived_from IS NOT NULL`), and its NO_PRODUCER list is explicitly "derived from CLAUDE.md §15", the unbuilt list. The finding's "a renderer added later will reconstruct it" is speculation about a renderer that does not exist; the column existing is precisely what makes reconstruction unnecessary when one is built.

(3) The one place pass 2 reaches a human states the label rather than omitting it: server/scripts/resolve.ts:212-216 prints "Every row is labelled `Inferred` and none says Documented. This build has no search…". That cannot diverge from storage — `honesty TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'Inferred'` (024:67) with a single writer that passes the literal (resolveProduct.ts:327), so no DB state makes the sentence false. Nothing is silently unlabelled anywhere.

(4) The repo names this exact shape as deliberate elsewhere, on the same reasoning: server/src/engine/confirm.ts:22-33 — "The `adopted` path has no production caller yet… It is constructed in tests and nowhere else, and by rule 11 that means this half is not yet proven by use… The guard has to be in place before the temptation, or the first author to reach for it will find nothing in the way." `object_provenance.honesty_label` (confirm.ts:131) is likewise written and never SELECTed. A schema column provisioned ahead of its renderer is the storage form of that norm, and CLAUDE.md §10 ("Longitudinal schema from the first commit") and §15's convention both cover it.

This is not the signature failure class: in every recorded instance a live reader returned a wrong or missing answer. Here the value is a build-wide constant identical to its own column default, reachable via a populated FK, with no reader in existence to be misled.

refutedTitles.title: `product_resolutions.honesty` is stamped as a SQL string literal and read by nothing — not by any renderer, not by a test — so the label the column exists to make travel does not travel.
killedBy:
REFUTED — the claim is factually wrong on its central assertion and defended by comments where it points.

1. THE CLAIM'S OWN FALSIFICATION CRITERION IS MET. It states it "would be disproved by any SELECT naming the column" and that `grep -rn honesty server/src server/scripts server/test` yields no read. That SELECT exists and that grep does yield a read:

server/test/resolve-product.test.ts:193-198
    const row = db.prepare('SELECT product, kind, honesty, resolved FROM product_resolutions').get() as {
      product: string; kind: string; honesty: string; resolved: number
    }
    assert.deepEqual(row, {
      product: 'Burcam Series 600 captive-air pressure tank', kind: 'equipment', honesty: 'Inferred', resolved: 1,
    })

That is a SELECT naming the column and a deepEqual asserting the stored value. It runs and passes — I ran `npx tsx --test server/test/resolve-product.test.ts`: 20 tests, 20 pass, 0 skipped. The column is also written in the storage-refusal test at resolve-product.test.ts:279. The evidence grep quoted in the claim scanned `server/src server/scripts` only, then concluded "not by a test."

2. THE "WHY IT MATTERS" PREMISE IS FALSE ON THE SCHEMA. The claim says "the first renderer of a plate-derived object will have to reconstruct the label." It will not — there is a live FK:

server/src/db/migrations/025_object_lanes.sql:32
    ALTER TABLE objects ADD COLUMN resolution_id TEXT REFERENCES product_resolutions(id);

025:17-19 argues exactly this: "`resolution_id` IS WHAT MAKES `plate` CHECKABLE. A plate-derived object with no resolution behind it is a claim about provenance with nothing supporting it, so the lane and its evidence arrive together or not at all." It is populated in production by pass 3 — server/src/ai/tasks/matchComplete.ts:557 inserts `derived_from, resolution_id, model_read, parent_object_id`. A renderer reaches `honesty` by join. The path is not severed, which is what the signature failure class requires.

3. THE BEHAVIOUR IS ARGUED AS DELIBERATE IN THE EXACT LINES CITED. server/src/db/migrations/024_product_resolutions.sql:65-66 — "Only ever `Inferred` in this build. The column exists so the value travels with the row rather than being reconstructed by whoever renders it." That is a write-time storage decision anticipating a future reader, and it is CLAUDE.md doctrine 1 verbatim: "This makes provenance a property of storage rather than a feature someone must remember to maintain." lookup.ts:186-194 and resolveProduct.ts:16-31 make the same argument for why `Documented` is absent.

4. THE ABSENCE OF A PRODUCTION READER IS THE ABSENCE OF A PRODUCT, NOT A BROKEN PATH. The intended consumer does not exist yet and CLAUDE.md says so on the record: §15 lists "Rendering the binder itself — Nothing. The gap report and the session plan render; the binder does not," and §16 says identification pass 4 (condition) does not exist. §15's rule is that such rows are "real, wanted, and correctly not built yet."

5. THE DRIFT SUB-POINT DOES NOT REACH 019's CLASS. Migration 019_objects_actor.sql:10-13 names "a hand-maintained restatement of something the data already knows." `honesty` has exactly one value and no data-derived source to derive from — there is nothing the data knows that the literal restates. `Honesty = 'Inferred'` (lookup.ts:196) is the only type, there is one INSERT site (resolveProduct.ts:324-327), and both 024:21-24 and lookup.ts:192-194 rule that `Documented` and `source_url` arrive in the same change or not at all. The only soft spot I found is that 024 has no CHECK constraint on `honesty` (it has one on `resolved` at :76) — but that is not the finding as stated, and the single hardcoded INSERT makes any other value unwritable today.

refutedTitles.title: The whole operating-state capability — table, append-only triggers, engine module and tests — has no writer and no caller anywhere in the running system.
killedBy:
The mechanical facts are TRUE and I reconfirmed each independently: `grep -rn operatingState server/src server/scripts web/src` returns 0; `grep -rn object_states` over the same trees returns nothing; only `server/test/operating-state.test.ts` touches the table. But three separate defences kill the finding.

1. IT IS DECLARED BY NAME, ON THE DAY IT SHIPPED, UNDER A HEADING TITLED "What is NOT built, by intent". docs/HouseSteady_Binder-Builder_Note_Frame-Bracket-Measurement_2026-08-11.md:187 — "**Nothing writes an `object_states` row yet.** The desk surface that would is unbuilt. **Said plainly, because a table with a reader and no writer is the declared-and-unconsumed class from the other end** — the difference is that this one's writer is a screen a person uses, not a pass." That names the exact failure class the finding invokes and pre-empts it. It is precisely the labelling CLAUDE.md §15 demands ("the fix is not vigilance, it is labelling"). The commit is corroborating: `a6984ac ... operating state schemad` (2026-08-11) — schemad, not built.

2. THE §15 ARGUMENT FAILS ON §15's OWN SCOPE. §15 is titled "What **this file** describes that nothing yet implements"; its table enumerates CLAUDE.md's own described-but-unbuilt doctrine, and its stated failure mode requires the stale sentence to be in CLAUDE.md, "read first by every new session… repeated into a cut". `grep -in "operating state|object_states|deliberately off" CLAUDE.md` returns nothing — operating state is not described in CLAUDE.md at all, so it cannot be a §15 row. §16 is the section for decisions binding here that live only in a /docs note, and it is explicitly "pointers, not doctrine".

3. THE "LIVE FAILURE MODE" IS FACTUALLY WRONG — the claim's strongest limb, and it fails hardest. It asserts "nothing in the pipeline consults `suppressesCare`, so a care package for a deliberately-off appliance is exactly what would render." But `grep -rn careCategories server/src server/scripts web/src` returns hits ONLY inside server/src/engine/classFrame.ts, where they are used solely for vocabulary validation (`checkVocabulary` at :318-336, `checkCareAudience` at :401). No code anywhere builds, proposes or renders a care package for an object. `suppressesCare` has nothing to suppress because the care-proposal step does not exist; nothing could render a care package for the geothermal-preheat water heater today. Identically, `doNotOperateLine` "rides a trades brief" — grep for trades brief across server/src, server/scripts, web/src and schema returns only operatingState.ts's own three comment lines. No trades brief exists either.

So this is deliberate pre-wiring for an unbuilt desk surface, disclosed in the note that shipped it using the vocabulary of the very failure class alleged. The migration header (023_operating_state.sql:1-44) also never claims a writer — it argues only why state is a table not a column and why the absent `generation_id` is a wall against a model writing state.

I confirmed the finder's mechanical facts and could not refute them on reachability. Exhaustive checks: `grep -rn "operatingState" server web package.json` (non-node_modules) returns exactly one line — `server/test/operating-state.test.ts:15: } from '../src/engine/operatingState.js'`. The defect FRAMING is what fails, on two independent counts.

(1) It is explicitly declared deliberate, in the finder's own terms. `docs/HouseSteady_Binder-Builder_Note_Frame-Bracket-Measurement_2026-08-11.md:187`:

Same for the migration: server/src/db/migrations/012_active_items.sql:57-63 is the header of `CREATE TABLE audit_carried_items` (line 69), and its next paragraph is "THIS IS NOT `audit_slots` AND MUST NOT BE MERGED WITH IT."

refutedTitles.title: `active_items.origin` admits 'received' and 'computed'; the only INSERT hardcodes 'received', so the reader's `origin = 'received'` filter is a no-op and two comments assert a write that never happens.
killedBy:
The factual half is right and the consequential half is wrong: the computed origin is both computed AND reachable by readers, in a persisted column, and the mixed case is exercised end to end by a passing test — so this is not the "value computed, reader cannot reach it" shape.

What I confirmed. `grep` repo-wide finds exactly one writer of `active_items` (server/src/import/persist.ts:342) and one reader (server/src/audit/activeItems.ts:196-197), and nothing sets origin to 'computed' in SQL. I ran it: imported `fixtures/reference/` through `runImport`, then `runAudit`. `SELECT origin, COUNT(*) FROM active_items GROUP BY origin` → `[]`; `activeItemSet` → `{ received: 0, computed: 39 }`; `SELECT origin, COUNT(*) FROM audit_carried_items GROUP BY origin` → `[{ origin: 'computed', n: 20 }]`. The table is empty in production for a further reason the finding does not mention: server/src/import/adapters/v3.ts:294 hardcodes `activeItems: []`, so the sole writer receives nothing on any real import. Both arms are unreachable today, not one.

Why that is the design and not the defect.

1. The computed origin is persisted where a derived claim belongs. server/src/audit/run.ts:384-391 writes `origin` per row into `audit_carried_items` straight from `item.origin`, under a comment at run.ts:379-381: "stored for the same reason `audit_slots` is: a rendered gap report has to be reproducible... rather than a re-run against today's config." That is an attributed, reproducible, per-row record of the computed claim, tied to the audit run that made it. `active_items` is the import's mirror of what the field declared; `audit_carried_items` is the builder's derivation. Doctrine 1 — imports stored verbatim, every builder change a separate record pointing at the original — argues for exactly that split, not against it.

2. The origin is also stated to a human on every run. server/src/audit/carriedItems.ts:244-248 pushes the breakdown unconditionally: "active item set: 0 received from the field, 39 computed here", under "a stream that does not say so lets a locally-derived 'was due' pass as the field app's own answer". This is the artifact Amendment 1 §A2 specified (docs/…Increment-4_Build-Spec_Amendment-1_2026-07-30.md:27). Nothing about it is unreachable.

3. `AND origin = 'received'` is not a dead predicate, it is the wall. If a computed row ever landed in that table, `fromReceived` (activeItems.ts:262-289) would relabel it `origin: 'received'` and stamp `certain: true, source: 'field'` — laundering a locally derived "was due" into the field app's own answer, which is doctrine 2 verbatim. The clause makes that structurally impossible before anything can hit it. "Deleting it changes no test result" is what a correctly placed wall looks like, and this repo builds those on purpose.

4. The mixed case IS exercised, at the layer that has readers. server/test/active-item-set.test.ts:145 — 'reports the origin breakdown when a property holds both kinds' — builds one import with a received set and a second with none and asserts `origins.received > 0 && origins.computed > 0`. Line 79 asserts both paths produce the same downstream shape, differing only in origin. The claim that the mixed case "has never been exercised" is true only of table rows nothing reads.

5. Not persisting is the coherent reading of the v3 branch's own status. activeItems.ts:327-330: "A proving exercise, not the production path... the zone-audit oracle checks it against the field app's own numbers on every closed zone. The moment v4 arrives this branch stops running for new imports" — matching CLAUDE.md §8. Freezing a derivation that is still being corrected against an oracle into the import's mirror table would be worse, not better, than recomputing it from the immutable per-import `config_snapshots`. The test file's own architecture note (active-item-set.test.ts:22-25) states the built seam plainly: "`persistImport` reads `canonical.activeItems` without knowing which version produced it, and `activeItemSet` prefers received rows over computing."

On the persist.ts comment: "the audit computes the set and writes `computed` rows instead" is accurate about the audit — it does write rows marked computed, 20 of them, measured above. Only the destination is left implicit.

The claim's mechanics check out but its consequence does not: the 'computed' origin is fully reachable, persisted and asserted — one table over, in the same migration.

VERIFIED TRUE: a raw grep over every file (excluding node_modules/.git) returns six `active_items` hits total — server/src/import/persist.ts:342 (the only writer, hardcoding 'received'), server/src/audit/activeItems.ts:197 (the only reader, `... WHERE import_id = ? AND origin = 'received'`), migration 012 lines 18/51/54, and one test-registry mention at server/test/operators.test.ts:64. No dynamic SQL builds the table name. I patched out `AND origin = 'received'` and ran all 1224 tests: one failure, server/test/carried-items.test.ts:288 (expected 'not-accessible', got 'certified'), and it is caused by a PRE-EXISTING uncommitted edit in the working tree to server/src/report/clientVoice.ts (GapLabel widened with 'certified'; line 168 returns `label: 'certified'`) — not by my patch. So the clause is inert today, as claimed. File restored.

WHY IT IS REFUTED ANYWAY — the value is reachable:
1. server/src/audit/activeItems.ts:360 mints `origin: 'computed'`; server/src/audit/carriedItems.ts:217 carries `origin: item.origin` onto every carried row; server/src/audit/run.ts:384-391 PERSISTS it — `INSERT INTO audit_carried_items (... origin, status, ...)` with `item.dueSince.at, item.origin, item.status`. The finder measured those 60 rows themselves and read them as evidence of absence; they are the storage.
2. A human-facing reader exists: server/src/audit/carriedItems.ts:244-249 — `active item set: ${active.origins.received} received from the field, ${active.origins.computed} computed here`, with the comment "a stream that does not say so lets a locally-derived 'was due' pass as the field app's own answer". server/test/carried-items.test.ts:80 asserts that exact line.
3. "The mixed case has never been exercised" is false. server/test/active-item-set.test.ts:145-159 persists a v4-shaped activeItems[] on one import, runImports a v3 export as a second visit on the same property, and asserts `set.origins.received > 0 && set.origins.computed > 0`. I reproduced it out-of-band: `after v4-shaped persist, rows by origin: [{origin:'received', n:2}]`, then `activeItemSet origins: { received: 2, computed: 39 }`. The mixed property works today; nothing waits on v4.
4. The filter is a correctness guard, not dead weight. server/src/audit/activeItems.ts:204-206 branches on `declared.length > 0`. If a computed row ever sat in active_items without the filter, `fromReceived` (line 275) would stamp `origin: 'received'` on it — laundering a local derivation into the field's own answer, which is precisely what server/test/active-item-set.test.ts:70 forbids ("a received set is not supplemented by a computed one — that would be two answers"). Removing it is the hazard; keeping it is depth.
5. Not writing computed rows into active_items is defensible under Doctrine 1, not an oversight: the table is keyed `UNIQUE (import_id, scope_kind, COALESCE(scope_zone_id,''), COALESCE(scope_pin_id,''), item_id)` (012:51-53) and written with INSERT OR IGNORE, so builder-derived rows filed under an import_id that declared none would collide with, and be indistinguishable from, a later real v4 import's rows. Derived rows belong in the audit run's own table — which migration 012:96-98 creates fifteen lines below with `origin TEXT NOT NULL` and the comment "Which import first made this item due, and the origin of that claim." Note also that server/test/doctrine.test.ts:134-137 lists CAPTURED_TABLES without active_items, so nothing forbids the write; it simply is not where the design put it.

refutedTitles.title: A column with nothing in it is dropped from the client HTML entirely, so "Missing from you" can vanish from a signed gap report with no statement in its place.
killedBy:
The behaviour is mandated verbatim by the build spec, and the record does not drop anything.

1. The spec orders exactly this. /home/user/housesteady-builder/docs/HouseSteady_Binder-Builder_Increment-4_Build-Spec_2026-07-30.md:75 (§1d "'Missing from you' ships, and ships honestly"): "The column could ship empty, or it could ship as a manually-entered list the concierge types from the intake form. **Ship it manual.** ... **What it must not do is render an empty column with a heading, which reads as *you owe us nothing*.**" The filter at server/src/report/render.ts:317-318 — `.filter((c) => c.groups.length > 0 || c.typed.length > 0)` — is that sentence implemented. The finding quotes the same §1d rule as the thing the code contradicts; read whole, §1d is the instruction to do precisely what line 318 does. Wanting a stand-in sentence in the empty column's place is a third option §1d considered neither and chose against ("two readings, and I mean the second").

2. The rationale is in the code, in the two modules that own the two halves. server/src/report/draft.ts:10-20 quotes §1d and then states the built mitigation: "So the column ships as rows a concierge types, carrying provenance `human-entered`". web/src/pages/GapReport.tsx:8-13 repeats it, and GapReport.tsx:236-243 is the mitigation working — the desk screen is where the empty column is shown, with "Nothing has been asked of the client yet. Type what they owe — the deed, permits, the well record, prior inspections." The design puts the empty-column moment in front of the human before signing, not in front of the client after. The claim treats "desk-side only" as the defect; it is the chosen location.

3. The doctrine-6 argument fails on the facts. render.ts:168 composes `draft.columns.map(...)` and draft.ts:328 always yields all three COLUMNS, so every edition stores all three — including empty ones — in `report_editions.composition` (render.ts:232-241), read back by `editions()` (render.ts:382-396) and served at server/src/index.ts:937. I ran the claim's own probe (import → runAudit → buildDraft → signEdition on the reference fixture, from /home/user/housesteady-builder/server): `h2 in html: [ 'Missing from us' ]` — the finding's observable reproduces — but the stored edition record reads `[{missing-from-you, groups:0, typed:0}, {missing-from-us, groups:2, typed:0}, {triggered-flags, groups:0, typed:0}]`. The column is omitted from one rendering of the edition, not dropped from the edition. Nothing is silently lost; the emptiness is reachable in the signed record and over the API, which is the opposite of the failure class being hunted.

The finding is a disagreement with a ratified spec ruling about how an empty column should read to a client, argued without the paragraph that ruled it. It is not a defect.

I reproduced the probe (import -> runAudit -> buildDraft -> signEdition on both committed fixtures, temp file since deleted): with no typed rows the stored HTML carries one <h2> ("Missing from us") and no "Missing from you"/"Triggered flags"; adding one manual row restores the heading. So the observations are accurate. The finding still fails, for three reasons. (1) The behaviour is the ratified spec's own instruction, not a contradiction of it: docs/HouseSteady_Binder-Builder_Increment-4_Build-Spec_2026-07-30.md:75 reads "**Ship it manual.** ... What it must not do is render an empty column with a heading, which reads as *you owe us nothing*." The filter at server/src/report/render.ts:318 (`.filter((c) => c.groups.length > 0 || c.typed.length > 0)`) implements that prohibition literally. The finder cites the same sentence (quoted at server/src/report/draft.ts:12-15) as the rule broken, but the sentence forbids the heading-with-nothing, which is precisely what the filter prevents; the "print a sentence in its place" third option appears nowhere in the spec, and CLAUDE.md §12 gives the spec the detail call. (2) The empty case IS handled at the decision point, not merely somewhere desk-side: web/src/pages/GapReport.tsx:84-104 puts the "Sign and render" button on the same page that maps draft.columns at :143 and prints, at :236-244, "Nothing has been asked of the client yet. Type what they owe - the deed, permits, the well record, prior inspections." A concierge signing an empty column was shown that it was empty, and what to type, at the moment of signing - the desk proposes, a person confirms. (3) Nothing is dropped from the record, so doctrine 6 is not engaged: signEdition builds `columns` from draft.columns unfiltered (server/src/report/render.ts:168-192) and my probe printed the stored composition as `missing-from-you[g=0,t=0] missing-from-us[g=2,t=0] triggered-flags[g=0,t=0]`; it persists in report_editions.composition and is readable via editions() (server/src/report/render.ts:390-407) and GET /api/properties/:id/report/editions (server/src/index.ts:936). I did confirm the finder's search was otherwise sound: document() in render.ts:335-378 is the only client renderer (other occurrences of the column titles are only draft.ts:138-140, audit/carriedItems.ts:57, doctrine.test.ts:808, web/src/api.ts:545), and only two RenderRefused codes exist (render.ts:151, 161), neither per-column.

coverageNotes.lens: Field 6 seam readiness — the IMPORT path (server/src/import/**, and the two call planners downstream of it)
coverageNotes.note:
WHAT I COVERED. Read all thirteen files in server/src/import/**, plus the two downstream call planners (engine/identify.ts, engine/assembly.ts + engine/plan.ts), pass/thumbs.ts, ai/image.ts, ai/worker.ts, ai/queue.ts, the migration set, and doctrine.test.ts's doctrine-1 block. Everything empirical above came from running the real walk export (fixtures/walk-2026-07-31) through `runImport` with the Field 6 additions grafted on exactly as the field team's example declares them, under `npx tsx`; probe files were written into server/test/, run, and deleted (`git status` clean but for the pre-existing `_scratch_seed.ts`).

DIRECT ANSWERS TO THE LENS QUESTIONS.

1. `position` is PRESERVED, not dropped — but only as bytes. `persist.ts:79` writes `raw_manifest: raw, // verbatim, whole, byte-for-byte what arrived`, and `runImport.ts:319` writes the same bytes to `<visitDir>/manifest.json`. My probe confirmed `raw_manifest holds "position": true`. The canonical shape does drop it: `v3.ts:218-238` enumerates media fields one by one and `position` is not among them. That drop is NOT a defect — it is argued and pinned by `doctrine.test.ts:911-929` ("keeps a field the canonical shape does not model"), whose comment states the design: *"The canonical shape is deliberately lossy — it models what the builder needs. That is only safe because the raw stays the record."* Doctrine 1 holds. What does not exist is any notice: I added both an unknown top-level section and a `positioned:false` refusal to a real export and `parseToCanonical` returned zero checks. Nothing in the import path reports that an export carried structure the builder did not read — the vocabulary pass surfaces unknown *values*, never unknown *keys*. I am not filing that as a defect because nothing yet consumes position and CLAUDE.md §15's convention covers it, but it is why the `positioned:false` refusal — the one state the field team says is worth investigating — will reach the desk invisibly until something is built.

2. An unknown `intent` FAILS OPEN and is stored (`persist.ts:224` → `media.capture_intent`, migration 022), and is treated safely as ordinary by `engine/identify.ts:249,292` (an unrecognised word can neither claim context authority nor drop a photograph). It is not counted, not marked unrecognised, and not on the report — finding 3. So: half of fail-open, which the module itself says is the whole failure.

3. `mime: application/json` is handled correctly where mime is actually consulted — `placeMedia` copies and checksums it like any file with no mime assumption (media.ts:131-184), `pass/thumbs.ts:129` returns `not-an-image` cleanly, and `web/src/pass/Decisions.tsx:342` does the same. It is handled wrongly in the two places that decide what a model looks at, both of which gate on `kind` — findings 1 and 2. Media is not assumed to be images broadly; it is assumed by exactly the two modules where the assumption is expensive.

4. WHAT EXISTS TO STORE POSITION: nothing. `media` (001_initial.sql:173-200, extended by 022) has no spatial column. `anchors.x/y` (001_initial.sql:164-165) is `normalized 0-1 relative to the canvas image` — 2D, per-pin, canvas-space, and unrelated to an ARKit world pose; reusing it would be the mistake. `objects` (017) carries `zone_id` and no coordinates. No table exists for zone geometry, so a floorplan or mesh payload has nowhere to go beyond the media row for its file.

5. SMALLEST CHANGE THAT MAKES POSITION SURVIVE WITHOUT BEING READ — four files, six lines, the same additive pattern migration 022 already established:
   (a) `server/src/db/migrations/027_media_position.sql`: `ALTER TABLE media ADD COLUMN position TEXT;` — verbatim JSON, no schema for it.
   (b) `server/src/import/manifest.ts:159` area: `position?: Record<string, unknown>` on `MediaRecord`, beside `intent?`.
   (c) `server/src/import/adapters/canonical.ts:147` area: `position: Record<string, unknown> | null` on `CanonicalMedia`; `server/src/import/adapters/v3.ts:229` area: `position: (x.position ?? null),`.
   (d) `server/src/import/persist.ts:196-237`: add `position` to the INSERT column list and `j(x.position)` to the values — `j` already null-safes (`db/index.ts:85`).
   Storing the object verbatim keeps all three states distinguishable without inventing a vocabulary: an object with `positioned: true`, an object with `positioned: false` plus `why`, and SQL NULL for absent. NULL for absent is the right encoding precisely because absence means inheritance from the container, not a gap. No reader, no branch, nothing downstream changes — and the container-is-positioned-if-any-frame-is rule stays unwritten until something needs it.

WHAT I COULD NOT REACH. I did not run the full 1224-test suite or the typecheck — every claim above is from a targeted run, not from the suite. There is no real Field 6 export in the repo, so every Field 6 observation is against the field team's hand-written example shape grafted onto a real export; if the real export differs (notably on `kind` for the two JSON captures, or on `files` vs `media`), findings 1, 2 and 5 change. I did not exercise `prepareImage` against an actual JSON file on disk — the ImageRefused path is read from the code, not observed, though `sharp().metadata()` on JSON has no other outcome. And I did not audit the field-side repo, which is where the `files[]` question is actually answered.

WHAT I COVERED. Every consumer that batches or groups media, traced to the line that selects: engine/identify.ts (the single planner all three vision passes share), ai/tasks/identify.ts, readSurfaces.ts, matchComplete.ts, nameplate.ts, routing.ts, pinType.ts, ai/image.ts, ai/worker.ts + queue.ts (failure handling), engine/assembly.ts + plan.ts + completeness.ts + runRecord.ts, import/vocabulary.ts + report.ts, pass/thumbs.ts, plan/sessionPlan.ts, overlay/store.ts, engine/surfaces.ts, engine/reviewQueue.ts. Docs read: CLAUDE.md, the Verification Discipline note, the Session Plan v0 contract in full, migration 022. I ran the real exported functions under tsx rather than reasoning from the source (probes in the scratchpad), and read the walk fixture's manifest directly.

WHERE MEDIA IS SELECTED FOR A MODEL CALL — the exact line. server/src/engine/identify.ts:261, `if (m.kind !== null && IMAGE_KINDS.includes(m.kind))`. It filters on **kind**. It filters on **intent** only at line 249 and only for the literal `run-trace`. It never filters on **mime**, and mime is not even fetched (ai/tasks/identify.ts:205-218). A floorplan/mesh JSON at kind 'photo' is batched as a detail photograph and reaches `prepareImage`, which throws `ImageRefused` and takes the whole zone-batch job down. Finding 1.

DOES THE SESSION PLAN NEED `position`? Structurally, one field does and it is `typedPins[].priorUnitPhoto` — contract §6's whole argument is *"nothing in the field app can enforce consistent framing unaided and at hour three the concierge will not recall the angle"*, and `sections.priorUnitPhotographs`'s own sentence (sessionPlan.ts:765-768) is *"so the same object is photographed from the same position rather than differently every month."* Today it carries `{ mediaId, capturedAt, itemId }` — a picture to look at, no pose. Nothing else in the plan reads or needs position: `zones[]` is attributes, `carriedGaps[]` is item ids and dates, `monitorsDue`/`comparisonPositionsDue` are id pairs, `openConcerns` is `never[]`. Whether the field wants a pose there is the field session's call and a `planSchemaVersion`-additive question under §12 — I am reporting the seam, not proposing the field. What I did find is that the field is already wrong about *which photograph* (finding 6).

IS A PHOTOGRAPH'S LOCATION REPRESENTED ANYWHERE? No — not a photograph's. Two things carry a location and both are a **pin's**, both 2D, both normalised against a canvas image:
 · `anchors` (migrations/001_initial.sql:159-171; canonical.ts:121-128) — `{anchorId, pinId, canvasId, x, y}`, field-minted, bounds-warned at import/integrity.ts:182-199.
 · the `place` overlay (overlay/store.ts:71-78, 305-340) — the desk's own placement, same `{canvasId, x, y}` shape plus required `evidence` naming what the position was read from.
The relation to a 3D pose is that there isn't one. A canvas anchor answers *where on this picture is the marker*; an ARKit pose answers *where in the room was the camera*. The anchor has no camera, no depth, no frame of reference beyond one image, and `media` has no spatial column at all. `PlaceValue` also cannot be widened quietly: overlay/store.ts:327-334 hard-refuses anything outside [0,1] and requires a `canvasId` that resolves in `canvases`, so a pose would be a new overlay kind, not a wider `place`.

RANKING MACHINERY TO REUSE FOR "closest frame wins by surface.distance". Yes, and it is `adjudicateManufacturer` in server/src/engine/surfaces.ts:180-236. It is the repo's worked answer to *competing claims about one fact*, and its shape is the one a distance ranking needs: it returns `{ asserted, supportedBy, claims, competing, why }`; losers are **retained, not deleted** ("Losing is a position in a list, not an absence from it", surfaces.ts:176-178, written against Register #121 where one column with room for one answer let the last write win); and a tie **asserts nothing** rather than picking arbitrarily (`distinct.length > 1` → `asserted: null`). A naive `frames.sort(byDistance)[0]` reproduces exactly the bug that function exists to prevent. The other sorts I checked are not this shape and should not be reused: engine/identify.ts:279-280 (`inWalkOrder` — determinism, not preference), engine/assembly.ts:319-341 (`stableByCapturedAt`), engine/reviewQueue.ts:127-130 (label frequency), engine/lookup.ts:132-145 (`specificity: unit|line|family|none` — a *specificity* ladder for product strings, closer in spirit but about text, not geometry). Note also that `surfaces.ts` gives the safety property Field 6 will want verbatim: an unrecognised surface is not `nameplate`, so a word nobody has met cannot acquire authority — the same argument applies to an unrecognised intent and a missing `distance`.

TWO PARALLEL BATCHERS, ONE OF THEM DEAD. `engine/assembly.ts` + `plan.ts` + `completeness.ts` + `runRecord.ts` implement the same resolve-to-zone / subject-vs-context / split-into-batches logic as `engine/identify.ts`, with different rules — assembly derives role from `owner_kind` alone (plan.ts:203-221) and has never heard of `capture_intent`, so it would call a `room-shot` a subject and a `run-trace` an ordinary photograph. It is imported only by server/test/ (`grep -rn "engine/assembly|engine/plan.js|propertyReadiness|assembleImport" server/src/index.ts server/scripts` → nothing). `propertyReadiness` says in its own header that its consumer is unbuilt, so I did not report the cluster's unreachedness as a defect — but I did report the consequence that bites, which is that the doctrine scan pins the dead constant (finding 2). Anyone fixing finding 1 needs to touch both, or delete one.

WHAT I COULD NOT REACH. No API key, no real photographs, and I did not run the full suite or any live import — the probes exercised the exported functions directly. I did not verify against a real Field 6 export because none exists in this repo (`fixtures/` holds the reference and walk v3 exports; neither has `position`, and `media[]` keys union is mediaId, kind, owner, group, file, mime, bytes, sha256, capturedAt, source, durationMs). Everything about Field 6's wire shape in this report is taken from the lens briefing, not from an artifact, and the failures I describe are properties of this repo's consumers that hold for *any* non-image file arriving under kind 'photo' — that part does not depend on the briefing being exact. I did not audit the web front end, the report/render path, or the audit engine, none of which touch media selection for a model call.
